Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Unfold a folding sweater dryer and stand it on its legs

Set up the folding sweater dryer on the kitchen counter with the dexterous hand. It starts fully folded and stored underside up, its four legs folded between the two frame halves. Open the two halves flat about the pole hinge, open all four legs onto their stops, turn the open rack over and stand it on its four feet, then let go: success needs the fold angle at most 0.314 rad, every leg at least 1.571 rad, the rack upright within 10 degrees on all four feet and nothing else, untouched by the hand and still for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). Dropping the rack, pushing it off the counter, or letting it collapse or fall over after it stands ends the episode as a failure at once.

You control one dexterous hand mounted on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three serial revolute
joints, no arm). The stage and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under native force bounds;
lifting, turning and releasing the rack require physical contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten
2 ms physics substeps.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Both hands hang from the same six-axis wrist stage (origin above the counter), with the same wrist joints, ranges, gains and start targets.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

## Scene
The rack is a folding sweater dryer: two rectangular frame halves (each 0.33 m x 0.65 m, 0.205 kg) joined by a passive
pole hinge on the side rims (0 rad = open flat, pi rad = folded), each half with two offset 0.098 m legs on passive hinges
(0 rad = folded flat, 1.745 rad = 100 degrees = open stop, no latch: the stop lies 10 degrees past vertical, so the
standing rack's weight keeps an open leg open). The woven net is drawn only and has no collision. The rack is a free
body of 0.51 kg and starts fully folded and stored underside up, its legs sandwiched between the halves.

## Success and failure
The episode is evaluated after every control from simulator state only, in this order:

1. **Unfolded**: the fold angle is at most 0.314 rad (at least 90 % of the opening stroke) and each of the four leg
   angles is at least 1.571 rad (90 degrees, at least 90 % of the leg stroke).
2. **Standing** (only after stage 1): the stage-1 condition holds, the rack's up axis (the normal of the fixed half,
   legs pointing down) is tilted at most 10 degrees from vertical, all four feet touch the counter and no other rack
   part touches it.
3. **Released hold**: the stage-2 condition holds, no hand geometry touches the rack, and every rack body moves at most
   0.02 m/s and 0.2 rad/s (centre-of-mass velocities), for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success
   at that control.

A partly open rack, a rack on fewer than four feet, a rack resting on a frame part, or a rack that is still held never
counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when

- any rack collision part's centre is below the counter top (z < 0.75 m), outside the counter footprint
  x in [-0.13, 1.37] m, y in [-0.48, 0.48] m, or more than 0.9 m above the counter;
- the rack touches the floor or the counter cabinet;
- the rack touches neither the counter nor the hand while its centre of mass falls faster than 0.05 m/s (dropped);
- after stage 2: the rack tilts more than 20 degrees (fell over), or the fold angle exceeds 0.314 rad or any leg angle
  drops below 1.571 rad (collapsed);
- the physics becomes unstable, or 6000 controls pass without success.

Later actions cannot undo a failure. Only hand and wrist-stage actuator targets are allowed; there are no welds,
attachments, scripted object motion or object forces.
Full task description (original text, privileged setting; differs from the standard one)
# DexHand: Unfold a folding sweater dryer and stand it on its legs

Set up the folding sweater dryer on the kitchen counter with the dexterous hand. It starts fully folded and stored underside up, its four legs folded between the two frame halves. Open the two halves flat about the pole hinge, open all four legs onto their stops, turn the open rack over and stand it on its four feet, then let go: success needs the fold angle at most 0.314 rad, every leg at least 1.571 rad, the rack upright within 10 degrees on all four feet and nothing else, untouched by the hand and still for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). Dropping the rack, pushing it off the counter, or letting it collapse or fall over after it stands ends the episode as a failure at once.

You control one dexterous hand mounted on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three serial revolute
joints, no arm). The stage and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under native force bounds;
lifting, turning and releasing the rack require physical contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten
2 ms physics substeps.

## Scene
The rack is a folding sweater dryer: two rectangular frame halves (each 0.33 m x 0.65 m, 0.205 kg, tube rims, end
poles and corner housings; the woven net between the rims is drawn only and has no collision) joined by a passive
pole hinge on the two side rims (`fold_hinge`: 0 rad = open flat, pi rad = folded; damping 0.001 N m s/rad, dry
friction 0.0005 N m). Each half carries two offset legs (0.025 kg, 0.098 m long, ball foot) on passive hinges
`fixed_leg_l_hinge`, `fixed_leg_r_hinge`, `moving_leg_l_hinge`, `moving_leg_r_hinge` (0 rad = folded flat against the
frame, 1.745 rad = 100 degrees = open stop; damping 0.03 N m s/rad, dry friction 0.003 N m). There is no latch: an
open leg stays open because its stop is 10 degrees past vertical, so the weight of the standing rack presses it onto the
stop. The rack is a free body of 0.51 kg. It starts fully folded and stored underside up on the counter (the legs of both
halves are sandwiched between them), exactly as in the scene's storage pose. The counter top is at z = 0.75 m and spans
x in [-0.13, 1.37] m, y in [-0.48, 0.48] m; the folded rack lies near (0.30, 0.0). Geometry, masses and contact
parameters are in `/opt/tools/scene.py` and `/opt/tools/task.json`.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Both hands hang from the same six-axis wrist stage (origin above the counter), with the same wrist joints, ranges, gains and start targets.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `28` wide for `sharpa` and `26` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control. The first six entries are the wrist-stage targets, identical for both hands:
`wrist_x, wrist_y, wrist_z` (metres) and `wrist_rx, wrist_ry, wrist_rz` (radians, serial XYZ joints, not a quaternion).
The three prismatic joints are offsets of the hand mount from the stage origin (0.62, 0, 0.75) m along the world axes
(ranges x [-0.85, 0.85], y [-0.6, 0.6], z [-0.05, 1.0] m; rx and rz [-3.3, 3.3], ry [-1.6, 1.6] rad). At zero rotation
the hand hangs palm down with the fingers along +x and the thumb toward +y. The finger targets follow in native actuator
order, in radians:

- `sharpa`: 28 values, the six wrist targets and 22 Sharpa Wave finger targets `right_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `right_pinky_DIP`.
- `wuji`: 26 values, the same six wrist targets and 20 Wuji Hand 2.2 finger targets `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3`,
  `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_MFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_RFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_LFJ0..3`.

Every target must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`. Both hands start from the same wrist targets (the hand
0.3 m to the -y side of the stage origin, 0.45 m above the counter, fingers open); the frozen start pose of each hand is
in `task.json` (`initial_targets`).

## Success and failure
The episode is evaluated after every control from simulator state only, in this order:

1. **Unfolded**: the fold angle is at most 0.314 rad (at least 90 % of the opening stroke) and each of the four leg
   angles is at least 1.571 rad (90 degrees, at least 90 % of the leg stroke).
2. **Standing** (only after stage 1): the stage-1 condition holds, the rack's up axis (the normal of the fixed half,
   legs pointing down) is tilted at most 10 degrees from vertical, all four feet touch the counter and no other rack
   part touches it.
3. **Released hold**: the stage-2 condition holds, no hand geometry touches the rack, and every rack body moves at most
   0.02 m/s and 0.2 rad/s (centre-of-mass velocities), for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success
   at that control.

A partly open rack, a rack on fewer than four feet, a rack resting on a frame part, or a rack that is still held never
counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when

- any rack collision part's centre is below the counter top (z < 0.75 m), outside the counter footprint
  x in [-0.13, 1.37] m, y in [-0.48, 0.48] m, or more than 0.9 m above the counter;
- the rack touches the floor or the counter cabinet;
- the rack touches neither the counter nor the hand while its centre of mass falls faster than 0.05 m/s (dropped);
- after stage 2: the rack tilts more than 20 degrees (fell over), or the fold angle exceeds 0.314 rad or any leg angle
  drops below 1.571 rad (collapsed);
- the physics becomes unstable, or 6000 controls pass without success.

Later actions cannot undo a failure. Only hand and wrist-stage actuator targets are allowed; there are no welds,
attachments, scripted object motion or object forces.

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 26)`
for `wuji`, at most 6000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Put a folded letter into an envelope

Put the folded letter into the envelope. A tri-folded A4 letter (a stiff 99 x 210 x 2 mm card, 5 g) lies flat on the desk at (0.48, -0.14) m; an empty DL wallet envelope (110 x 220 mm, 6 g) lies flat at (0.48, 0.16) m with its open mouth along its +X long edge and the open flap on the desk beyond the mouth. The envelope is a pocket: back and front walls 4 mm apart, permanent 3 mm side seams (narrowing to nothing over the last 10 mm before the mouth) and a 4 mm bottom seam, and a 30 mm elastic mouth lip that starts closed (flush with the front wall, 4 mm above the back wall); a fingertip or the letter can lift it. Both objects are free and move only through contact. Move the letter to the mouth and feed it in through the mouth, then let go. Stages, measured on the letter's four corners (centre plane) in the envelope's own frame (origin at the envelope centre on the desk, x towards the mouth, mouth line x = 55 mm): (1) the letter is at the mouth: both leading corners are at least 10 mm past the mouth line, inside the side seams (|y| <= 107.6 mm) and between the walls (height 1.2 to 4.4 mm) while both trailing corners are still outside the mouth line; (2) the letter is inserted: at most 5 % of its 99 mm length (4.95 mm) is outside the mouth line, all four corners are inside the side seams, in front of the bottom seam (x >= -51.6 mm) and between the walls; (3) released: stage 2 holds with no contact between the hand and the letter or the envelope, and both objects at rest (linear speed <= 0.01 m/s, angular speed <= 0.2 rad/s), for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). Stages count in order; the episode ends with success when the hold completes. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when the letter or the envelope falls below the desk top (origin z < 0.698 m), touches the floor, is dropped (touches nothing - no hand, desk or envelope - while its centre of mass falls faster than 0.1 m/s), leaves the desk (origin x outside [0.18, 0.78] m, y outside [-0.40, 0.40] m, or z > 1.00 m), when the letter is pressed through an envelope wall, seam or the mouth lip (any point of the letter's mid-plane inside one of them) or interpenetrates the envelope by more than 0.7 mm, when the envelope is pushed more than 5 cm from its start or tilted more than 0.35 rad, when the robot's arm, stand or parked left hand touches the letter or the envelope, or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed; no object teleports, welds, scripted object motion or object forces. The episode allows at most 6000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure. Simplifications: the folded letter is simulated as one rigid 2 mm card with rounded fold edges (paper bending is not simulated); the envelope is one rigid pocket whose seams are solid walls, whose open flap is a thin wedge on the desk and whose mouth lip is a passive spring hinge; the flap is never sealed. The hand is on the right arm of a dual-arm robot standing at the desk's +x edge; the left arm stays parked.

You control the right arm and hand of a fixed Tianji Marvin dual-arm robot (a stand with two seven-joint arms and a
dexterous hand on each wrist). The robot stands at the desk's +x edge (base origin (1.15, -0.25, 0.10) m, facing -x; its base plate stands on the floor at z = 0); the
left arm is parked beside the torso and only the right arm and hand do the task. Arm joints and fingers are position
servos in the physics engine under native force bounds; pressing, sliding, pushing and releasing require physical
contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Each row starts with the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (left arm J1-J7, then right arm J1-J7), followed by the left hand's finger targets and then the right hand's (22 per hand for `sharpa`, 20 per hand for `wuji`); the left arm is parked and only the right arm/hand perform the task.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`58` for `sharpa`, `54` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

# DexHand: Put a folded letter into an envelope

Put the folded letter into the envelope. A tri-folded A4 letter (a stiff 99 x 210 x 2 mm card, 5 g) lies flat on the desk at (0.48, -0.14) m; an empty DL wallet envelope (110 x 220 mm, 6 g) lies flat at (0.48, 0.16) m with its open mouth along its +X long edge and the open flap on the desk beyond the mouth. The envelope is a pocket: back and front walls 4 mm apart, permanent 3 mm side seams (narrowing to nothing over the last 10 mm before the mouth) and a 4 mm bottom seam, and a 30 mm elastic mouth lip that starts closed (flush with the front wall, 4 mm above the back wall); a fingertip or the letter can lift it. Both objects are free and move only through contact. Move the letter to the mouth and feed it in through the mouth, then let go. Stages, measured on the letter's four corners (centre plane) in the envelope's own frame (origin at the envelope centre on the desk, x towards the mouth, mouth line x = 55 mm): (1) the letter is at the mouth: both leading corners are at least 10 mm past the mouth line, inside the side seams (|y| <= 107.6 mm) and between the walls (height 1.2 to 4.4 mm) while both trailing corners are still outside the mouth line; (2) the letter is inserted: at most 5 % of its 99 mm length (4.95 mm) is outside the mouth line, all four corners are inside the side seams, in front of the bottom seam (x >= -51.6 mm) and between the walls; (3) released: stage 2 holds with no contact between the hand and the letter or the envelope, and both objects at rest (linear speed <= 0.01 m/s, angular speed <= 0.2 rad/s), for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). Stages count in order; the episode ends with success when the hold completes. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when the letter or the envelope falls below the desk top (origin z < 0.698 m), touches the floor, is dropped (touches nothing - no hand, desk or envelope - while its centre of mass falls faster than 0.1 m/s), leaves the desk (origin x outside [0.18, 0.78] m, y outside [-0.40, 0.40] m, or z > 1.00 m), when the letter is pressed through an envelope wall, seam or the mouth lip (any point of the letter's mid-plane inside one of them) or interpenetrates the envelope by more than 0.7 mm, when the envelope is pushed more than 5 cm from its start or tilted more than 0.35 rad, when the robot's arm, stand or parked left hand touches the letter or the envelope, or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed; no object teleports, welds, scripted object motion or object forces. The episode allows at most 6000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure. Simplifications: the folded letter is simulated as one rigid 2 mm card with rounded fold edges (paper bending is not simulated); the envelope is one rigid pocket whose seams are solid walls, whose open flap is a thin wedge on the desk and whose mouth lip is a passive spring hinge; the flap is never sealed. The hand is on the right arm of a dual-arm robot standing at the desk's +x edge; the left arm stays parked.

You control the right arm and hand of a fixed Tianji Marvin dual-arm robot (a stand with two seven-joint arms and a
dexterous hand on each wrist). The robot stands at the desk's +x edge (base origin (1.15, -0.25, 0.10) m, facing -x; its base plate stands on the floor at z = 0); the
left arm is parked beside the torso and only the right arm and hand do the task. Arm joints and fingers are position
servos in the physics engine under native force bounds; pressing, sliding, pushing and releasing require physical
contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Each row starts with the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (left arm J1-J7, then right arm J1-J7), followed by the left hand's finger targets and then the right hand's (22 per hand for `sharpa`, 20 per hand for `wuji`); the left arm is parked and only the right arm/hand perform the task.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `58` wide for `sharpa` and `54` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control in native actuator order (`s.actuator_names`), radians:

- `sharpa`: 58 values: the 7 left-arm joint targets `SHOULDER_PITCH_L_J1_target, SHOULDER_ROLL_L_J2_target,
  ELBOW_PITCH_L_J3_target, ELBOW_YAW_L_J4_target, WRIST_PITCH_L_J5_target, WRIST_YAW_L_J6_target,
  WRIST_ROLL_L_J7_target`, the 7 right-arm joint targets (`..._R_J1_target` ... `..._R_J7_target`), then the 22
  left-hand and the 22 right-hand Sharpa Wave finger targets (`left_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `left_pinky_DIP`,
  `right_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `right_pinky_DIP`).
- `wuji`: 54 values: the same 14 arm targets, then the 20 left-hand and the 20 right-hand Wuji Hand 2.2 finger
  targets (`l_wuji_l_THJ0..3, FFJ0..3, MFJ0..3, RFJ0..3, LFJ0..3`, then the same for `r_wuji_r_`).

Every target must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`. Both hands start from the same arm targets (`task.json`
`initial_targets`); keep the left arm parked (its start targets), it must not touch the letter or the envelope.

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 58)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 54)`
for `wuji`, at most 6000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

DexHand: Free-held cube layer reversal

Keep a free cube body steady while independently turning its top layer through an ordered quarter-turn reversal.
  • Original environment (the task's own code in its Docker image, MuJoCo 3.4.0), packaged reference actions, control rows counted from 0: Sharpa Wave: success after 450 controls (stages reached at control rows 356, 395 and 434); Wuji Hand 2.2: success after 940 controls (stages reached at control rows 326, 620 and 917). On this machine the start-state hash of the Sharpa Wave build differs from the one frozen in the task: the hash also covers small matrix products that numpy computes with the CPU's BLAS kernel, and 1 of their numbers rounds differently here (by at most 1 unit in the last place). With this machine's MuJoCo state untouched the frozen hash is reproduced when those products are rounded the other way (576 rounding variants tried), so the physics start state is bit for bit the recorded one; gate G0 counts as passed on that proof (build/efe/native/essential_cube_layer/sharpa/host_dependence.json). For the Wuji Hand 2.2 build the start-state hash equals the one frozen in the task in MuJoCo 3.4.0. The task's reset steps the physics, so under 3.8.0 the original code starts from that engine's own settled state, whose hash cannot equal the frozen one (the port's cross-engine runs start from the original engine's start state). The scene text built on our machine equals the one built in the image.
  • Same engine (the original's own engine, MuJoCo 3.4.0): the exported scene file, stepped by the port's own loop, gives exactly the bits of the original code: the full simulation state after every one of 8,231 controls, over the reference and 6 perturbed copies of it, for Sharpa Wave and Wuji Hand 2.2.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Free-held cube layer reversal

With the wrist locked, turn only the top layer +90 degrees, return it to zero, and turn it +90 degrees again. Stabilize the free cube body with other fingers; no external support or object actuation is allowed.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently
actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the verifier uses the frozen task's unrounded values, which differ from these only beyond the sixth significant digit). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `quarter_turn`: `1.4508 <= top_turn <= 1.6908`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `1 <= mechanism_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `return_zero`: `-0.12 <= top_turn <= 0.12`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `1 <= mechanism_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Stage `repeat_quarter_turn`: `1.4508 <= top_turn <= 1.6908`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `1 <= mechanism_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
4. Terminal hold after the last stage: `1.4508 <= top_turn <= 1.6908`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.12`, for 15 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 20`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.006`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.035`, `support == 0`, `0 <= body_drift <= 0.02`, `0 <= body_rotation <= 0.35`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered in that episode (a reset starts a new one: `## Episodes and resets`). Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `top_turn`: angle of the cube's top layer relative to its body, rad
- `base_contacts`: fingers in contact (> 0.005 N) with the object's body / controller shell
- `mechanism_contacts`: fingers in contact (> 0.005 N) with the moving mechanism (top layer / thumbstick)
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `support`: contacts (> 0.01 N) between a task object and the environment (table, fixtures)
- `body_drift`: displacement of the free object's body from its reset position, m
- `body_rotation`: rotation of the free object's body from its reset orientation, rad

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

# DexHand: Free-held cube layer reversal

With the wrist locked, turn only the top layer +90 degrees, return it to zero, and turn it +90 degrees again. Stabilize the free cube body with other fingers; no external support or object actuation is allowed.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently

change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `28` wide for `sharpa` and `26` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the exact numbers are in `catalog.json` in `/opt/tools`). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `quarter_turn`: `1.4508 <= top_turn <= 1.6908`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `1 <= mechanism_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `return_zero`: `-0.12 <= top_turn <= 0.12`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `1 <= mechanism_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Stage `repeat_quarter_turn`: `1.4508 <= top_turn <= 1.6908`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `1 <= mechanism_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
4. Terminal hold after the last stage: `1.4508 <= top_turn <= 1.6908`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.12`, for 15 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 20`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.006`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.035`, `support == 0`, `0 <= body_drift <= 0.02`, `0 <= body_rotation <= 0.35`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered. Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `top_turn`: angle of the cube's top layer relative to its body, rad
- `base_contacts`: fingers in contact (> 0.005 N) with the object's body / controller shell
- `mechanism_contacts`: fingers in contact (> 0.005 N) with the moving mechanism (top layer / thumbstick)
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `support`: contacts (> 0.01 N) between a task object and the environment (table, fixtures)
- `body_drift`: displacement of the free object's body from its reset position, m
- `body_rotation`: rotation of the free object's body from its reset orientation, rad

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for Sharpa or `(T, 26)`
for Wuji (at most 50,000 rows) and the `hand` it was made for, as written by `s.save_trajectory` (an archive
without `hand` is replayed as Sharpa), and `/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. Each row is one
control step: wrist x/y/z targets in metres, wrist XYZ Euler joint targets in radians, then the finger targets in
`s.actuator_names` order. Do not save object
states as the deliverable: the verifier executes the actions from the frozen start in one fresh process.
NaN, infinity, object arrays and malformed or oversized trajectories are rejected.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Fixed-wrist multi-axis marked sphere reorientation

With the wrist fixed, rotate the free marked sphere +90 degrees around palm-local Y, then +90 degrees around palm-local X from that pose, then return to its exact initial orientation. Maintain hand contact and avoid any external support throughout; stabilize each ordered checkpoint with at least two fingertips.

Palm-local axes belong to a frame fixed to the palm; with the wrist locked it is aligned with the world axes: +X points from the wrist toward the fingertips (world +x), +Y points across the palm from the thumb side toward the little-finger side (world +y), and +Z points out of the palm, which faces up (world +z). In the simulator it has the orientation of the `wrist_stage` body (the identity quaternion while the wrist is locked), not that of the palm link `right_hand_C_MC`, whose own axes are rotated relative to it. A turn about a palm-local axis is about that palm-fixed axis (it does not turn with the object), and a positive angle follows the right-hand rule: counterclockwise when seen from the positive end of the axis looking back toward the palm. So +90 degrees about Y carries the side of the sphere that faces up toward the fingertips, and +90 degrees about X carries the side that faces up toward the thumb side.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently
actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the verifier uses the frozen task's unrounded values, which differ from these only beyond the sixth significant digit). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `first_axis_quarter_turn`: `0 <= cube_error_1 <= 0.16`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `second_axis_quarter_turn`: `0 <= cube_error_2 <= 0.16`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Stage `return_to_initial`: `0 <= cube_error_3 <= 0.16`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
4. Terminal hold after the last stage: `0 <= cube_error_3 <= 0.16`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.06`, for 25 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 12`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.003`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.01`, `support == 0`, `0 <= object_displacement <= 0.07`, `0.18 <= object_height <= 0.6`, `object_hand_contacts >= 1`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered in that episode (a reset starts a new one: `## Episodes and resets`). Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `cube_error_1`: rotation between the marked sphere (palm frame) and its target after the first quarter turn, rad
- `contacts`: fingers whose fingertip pad touches a task object (> 0.01 N)
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `cube_error_2`: rotation between the marked sphere (palm frame) and its target after the second quarter turn, rad
- `cube_error_3`: rotation between the marked sphere (palm frame) and its reset orientation, rad
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `support`: contacts (> 0.01 N) between a task object and the environment (table, fixtures)
- `object_displacement`: object displacement from its reset position in the palm frame, m
- `object_height`: height of the object's centre above the world origin, m (the table top is at 0.10 m)
- `object_hand_contacts`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between the object and any hand link

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the exact numbers are in `catalog.json` in `/opt/tools`). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `first_axis_quarter_turn`: `0 <= cube_error_1 <= 0.16`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `second_axis_quarter_turn`: `0 <= cube_error_2 <= 0.16`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Stage `return_to_initial`: `0 <= cube_error_3 <= 0.16`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
4. Terminal hold after the last stage: `0 <= cube_error_3 <= 0.16`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.06`, for 25 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 12`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.003`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.01`, `support == 0`, `0 <= object_displacement <= 0.07`, `0.18 <= object_height <= 0.6`, `object_hand_contacts >= 1`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered. Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `cube_error_1`: rotation between the marked sphere (palm frame) and its target after the first quarter turn, rad
- `contacts`: fingers whose fingertip pad touches a task object (> 0.01 N)
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `cube_error_2`: rotation between the marked sphere (palm frame) and its target after the second quarter turn, rad
- `cube_error_3`: rotation between the marked sphere (palm frame) and its reset orientation, rad
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `support`: contacts (> 0.01 N) between a task object and the environment (table, fixtures)
- `object_displacement`: object displacement from its reset position in the palm frame, m
- `object_height`: height of the object's centre above the world origin, m (the table top is at 0.10 m)
- `object_hand_contacts`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between the object and any hand link

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for Sharpa or `(T, 26)`
for Wuji (at most 50,000 rows) and the `hand` it was made for, as written by `s.save_trajectory` (an archive
without `hand` is replayed as Sharpa), and `/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. Each row is one
control step: wrist x/y/z targets in metres, wrist XYZ Euler joint targets in radians, then the finger targets in
`s.actuator_names` order. Do not save object
states as the deliverable: the verifier executes the actions from the frozen start in one fresh process.
NaN, infinity, object arrays and malformed or oversized trajectories are rejected.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Held Joy-Con thumbstick sequence

With the wrist locked, keep the controller steady and move the joystick through left, front, right, back, then center, holding each checkpoint. Checkpoints are joint angles relative to the shell, not world tilt.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently
actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the verifier uses the frozen task's unrounded values, which differ from these only beyond the sixth significant digit). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `left`: `-0.4 <= joystick_x <= -0.2`, `-0.1 <= joystick_y <= 0.1`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `front`: `-0.1 <= joystick_x <= 0.1`, `0.2 <= joystick_y <= 0.4`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Stage `right`: `0.2 <= joystick_x <= 0.4`, `-0.1 <= joystick_y <= 0.1`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
4. Stage `back`: `-0.1 <= joystick_x <= 0.1`, `-0.4 <= joystick_y <= -0.2`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
5. Stage `center`: `-0.1 <= joystick_x <= 0.1`, `-0.1 <= joystick_y <= 0.1`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
6. Terminal hold after the last stage: `-0.08 <= joystick_x <= 0.08`, `-0.08 <= joystick_y <= 0.08`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.12`, for 15 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 20`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.006`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.035`, `support == 0`, `0 <= body_drift <= 0.02`, `0 <= body_rotation <= 0.35`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered in that episode (a reset starts a new one: `## Episodes and resets`). Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `joystick_x`: thumbstick gimbal angle about its first axis, rad
- `joystick_y`: thumbstick angle about its second axis, rad
- `base_contacts`: fingers in contact (> 0.005 N) with the object's body / controller shell
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `support`: contacts (> 0.01 N) between a task object and the environment (table, fixtures)
- `body_drift`: displacement of the free object's body from its reset position, m
- `body_rotation`: rotation of the free object's body from its reset orientation, rad

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `28` wide for `sharpa` and `26` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the exact numbers are in `catalog.json` in `/opt/tools`). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `left`: `-0.4 <= joystick_x <= -0.2`, `-0.1 <= joystick_y <= 0.1`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `front`: `-0.1 <= joystick_x <= 0.1`, `0.2 <= joystick_y <= 0.4`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Stage `right`: `0.2 <= joystick_x <= 0.4`, `-0.1 <= joystick_y <= 0.1`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
4. Stage `back`: `-0.1 <= joystick_x <= 0.1`, `-0.4 <= joystick_y <= -0.2`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
5. Stage `center`: `-0.1 <= joystick_x <= 0.1`, `-0.1 <= joystick_y <= 0.1`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
6. Terminal hold after the last stage: `-0.08 <= joystick_x <= 0.08`, `-0.08 <= joystick_y <= 0.08`, `1 <= base_contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.12`, for 15 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 20`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.006`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.035`, `support == 0`, `0 <= body_drift <= 0.02`, `0 <= body_rotation <= 0.35`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered. Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `joystick_x`: thumbstick gimbal angle about its first axis, rad
- `joystick_y`: thumbstick angle about its second axis, rad
- `base_contacts`: fingers in contact (> 0.005 N) with the object's body / controller shell
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `support`: contacts (> 0.01 N) between a task object and the environment (table, fixtures)
- `body_drift`: displacement of the free object's body from its reset position, m
- `body_rotation`: rotation of the free object's body from its reset orientation, rad

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for Sharpa or `(T, 26)`
for Wuji (at most 50,000 rows) and the `hand` it was made for, as written by `s.save_trajectory` (an archive
without `hand` is replayed as Sharpa), and `/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. Each row is one
control step: wrist x/y/z targets in metres, wrist XYZ Euler joint targets in radians, then the finger targets in
`s.actuator_names` order. Do not save object
states as the deliverable: the verifier executes the actions from the frozen start in one fresh process.
NaN, infinity, object arrays and malformed or oversized trajectories are rejected.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.
