Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Paper Mate palm-to-tripod pen regrasp

With the wrist fixed, move the unsupported pen 30 mm along its initial longitudinal axis relative to the palm, then turn its axis by 45 degrees and hold its marked grip band with thumb, index and middle fingertips. The initial pen rests against the central palm surfaces; the final pen must clear those central palm surfaces. All three named fingertips must contact the marked band. Other finger links may also contribute contact; an exclusive fingertip-only grasp is not required. No table support, other hand or whole-object release is allowed.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently
actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the verifier uses the frozen task's unrounded values, which differ from these only beyond the sixth significant digit). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `advance_pen`: `0.024 <= pen_axial <= 0.036`, `0 <= pen_angle <= 0.2`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `turn_and_tripod_grip`: `0.024 <= pen_axial <= 0.036`, `0.65 <= pen_angle <= 0.92`, `3 <= pen_grip_contacts <= 5`, `contact_thumb == 1`, `contact_index == 1`, `contact_middle == 1`, `pen_palm_contacts == 0`, `pen_grip_thumb == 1`, `pen_grip_index == 1`, `pen_grip_middle == 1`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Terminal hold after the last stage: `0.024 <= pen_axial <= 0.036`, `0.65 <= pen_angle <= 0.92`, `3 <= pen_grip_contacts <= 5`, `contact_thumb == 1`, `contact_index == 1`, `contact_middle == 1`, `pen_palm_contacts == 0`, `0 <= speed <= 0.06`, `pen_grip_thumb == 1`, `pen_grip_index == 1`, `pen_grip_middle == 1`, for 25 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 12`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.003`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.01`, `support == 0`, `0 <= object_displacement <= 0.07`, `0.18 <= object_height <= 0.6`, `object_hand_contacts >= 1`, `pen_initial_palm_contacts >= 1`, `0 <= pen_initial_horizontal_error <= 0.174533`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered in that episode (a reset starts a new one: `## Episodes and resets`). Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `pen_axial`: pen displacement along its reset axis in the palm frame, m
- `pen_angle`: angle between the pen axis and its reset axis in the palm frame, rad
- `contacts`: fingers whose fingertip pad touches a task object (> 0.01 N)
- `pen_grip_contacts`: fingers whose fingertip pad touches the pen inside the painted grip band (> 0.01 N)
- `contact_thumb`: see scene.py
- `contact_index`: see scene.py
- `contact_middle`: see scene.py
- `pen_palm_contacts`: palm contacts with the pen (> 0.01 N)
- `pen_grip_thumb`: see scene.py
- `pen_grip_index`: see scene.py
- `pen_grip_middle`: see scene.py
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `support`: contacts (> 0.01 N) between a task object and the environment (table, fixtures)
- `object_displacement`: object displacement from its reset position in the palm frame, m
- `object_height`: height of the object's centre above the world origin, m (the table top is at 0.10 m)
- `object_hand_contacts`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between the object and any hand link
- `pen_initial_palm_contacts`: palm contacts with the pen in the frozen reset (constant)
- `pen_initial_horizontal_error`: inclination of the pen in the frozen reset, rad (constant)

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).
Full task description (original text, privileged setting; differs from the standard one)
# DexHand: Paper Mate palm-to-tripod pen regrasp

With the wrist fixed, move the unsupported pen 30 mm along its initial longitudinal axis relative to the palm, then turn its axis by 45 degrees and hold its marked grip band with thumb, index and middle fingertips. The initial pen rests against the central palm surfaces; the final pen must clear those central palm surfaces. All three named fingertips must contact the marked band. Other finger links may also contribute contact; an exclusive fingertip-only grasp is not required. No table support, other hand or whole-object release is allowed.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently
actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `28` wide for `sharpa` and `26` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the exact numbers are in `catalog.json` in `/opt/tools`). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `advance_pen`: `0.024 <= pen_axial <= 0.036`, `0 <= pen_angle <= 0.2`, `2 <= contacts <= 5`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `turn_and_tripod_grip`: `0.024 <= pen_axial <= 0.036`, `0.65 <= pen_angle <= 0.92`, `3 <= pen_grip_contacts <= 5`, `contact_thumb == 1`, `contact_index == 1`, `contact_middle == 1`, `pen_palm_contacts == 0`, `pen_grip_thumb == 1`, `pen_grip_index == 1`, `pen_grip_middle == 1`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Terminal hold after the last stage: `0.024 <= pen_axial <= 0.036`, `0.65 <= pen_angle <= 0.92`, `3 <= pen_grip_contacts <= 5`, `contact_thumb == 1`, `contact_index == 1`, `contact_middle == 1`, `pen_palm_contacts == 0`, `0 <= speed <= 0.06`, `pen_grip_thumb == 1`, `pen_grip_index == 1`, `pen_grip_middle == 1`, for 25 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 12`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.003`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.01`, `support == 0`, `0 <= object_displacement <= 0.07`, `0.18 <= object_height <= 0.6`, `object_hand_contacts >= 1`, `pen_initial_palm_contacts >= 1`, `0 <= pen_initial_horizontal_error <= 0.174533`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered. Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `pen_axial`: pen displacement along its reset axis in the palm frame, m
- `pen_angle`: angle between the pen axis and its reset axis in the palm frame, rad
- `contacts`: fingers whose fingertip pad touches a task object (> 0.01 N)
- `pen_grip_contacts`: fingers whose fingertip pad touches the pen inside the painted grip band (> 0.01 N)
- `contact_thumb`: see scene.py
- `contact_index`: see scene.py
- `contact_middle`: see scene.py
- `pen_palm_contacts`: palm contacts with the pen (> 0.01 N)
- `pen_grip_thumb`: see scene.py
- `pen_grip_index`: see scene.py
- `pen_grip_middle`: see scene.py
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `support`: contacts (> 0.01 N) between a task object and the environment (table, fixtures)
- `object_displacement`: object displacement from its reset position in the palm frame, m
- `object_height`: height of the object's centre above the world origin, m (the table top is at 0.10 m)
- `object_hand_contacts`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between the object and any hand link
- `pen_initial_palm_contacts`: palm contacts with the pen in the frozen reset (constant)
- `pen_initial_horizontal_error`: inclination of the pen in the frozen reset, rad (constant)

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for Sharpa or `(T, 26)`
for Wuji (at most 50,000 rows) and the `hand` it was made for, as written by `s.save_trajectory` (an archive
without `hand` is replayed as Sharpa), and `/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. Each row is one
control step: wrist x/y/z targets in metres, wrist XYZ Euler joint targets in radians, then the finger targets in
`s.actuator_names` order. Do not save object
states as the deliverable: the verifier executes the actions from the frozen start in one fresh process.
NaN, infinity, object arrays and malformed or oversized trajectories are rejected.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Multi-turn encoder knob with fixed-wrist finger gait

Keep the wrist fixed. Rotate the rotary encoder knob to +720 degrees, then reverse to +360 degrees and hold it still. The real encoder cap has its actual rounded outer profile, normal surface friction and bearing resistance, and a passive unlimited-turn hinge. There is no task-object actuator or powered turning assistance. Maintain load-bearing hand contact throughout and perform at least four contact handoffs involving overlapping fingers.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently
actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the verifier uses the frozen task's unrounded values, which differ from these only beyond the sixth significant digit). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `two_forward_turns`: `12.4464 <= turn <= 12.6864`, `rotor_handoffs >= 4`, `1 <= rotor_fingers <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `one_reverse_turn`: `6.16319 <= turn <= 6.40319`, `1 <= rotor_fingers <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Terminal hold after the last stage: `6.16319 <= turn <= 6.40319`, `1 <= rotor_fingers <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.06`, for 25 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 12`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.003`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.01`, `rotor_hand_contacts >= 1`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered in that episode (a reset starts a new one: `## Episodes and resets`). Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `turn`: unwrapped knob angle, rad
- `rotor_handoffs`: finger-set handoffs on the knob (a new set sharing a finger with the previous one, stable 40 ms)
- `rotor_fingers`: fingers touching the knob (> 0.005 N)
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `rotor_hand_contacts`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between the knob and the hand

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).
Full task description (original text, privileged setting; differs from the standard one)
# DexHand: Multi-turn encoder knob with fixed-wrist finger gait

Keep the wrist fixed. Rotate the rotary encoder knob to +720 degrees, then reverse to +360 degrees and hold it still. The real encoder cap has its actual rounded outer profile, normal surface friction and bearing resistance, and a passive unlimited-turn hinge. There is no task-object actuator or powered turning assistance. Maintain load-bearing hand contact throughout and perform at least four contact handoffs involving overlapping fingers.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently
actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `28` wide for `sharpa` and `26` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the exact numbers are in `catalog.json` in `/opt/tools`). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `two_forward_turns`: `12.4464 <= turn <= 12.6864`, `rotor_handoffs >= 4`, `1 <= rotor_fingers <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
2. Stage `one_reverse_turn`: `6.16319 <= turn <= 6.40319`, `1 <= rotor_fingers <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
3. Terminal hold after the last stage: `6.16319 <= turn <= 6.40319`, `1 <= rotor_fingers <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.06`, for 25 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= speed <= 12`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.003`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.01`, `rotor_hand_contacts >= 1`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered. Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `turn`: unwrapped knob angle, rad
- `rotor_handoffs`: finger-set handoffs on the knob (a new set sharing a finger with the previous one, stable 40 ms)
- `rotor_fingers`: fingers touching the knob (> 0.005 N)
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `rotor_hand_contacts`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between the knob and the hand

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for Sharpa or `(T, 26)`
for Wuji (at most 50,000 rows) and the `hand` it was made for, as written by `s.save_trajectory` (an archive
without `hand` is replayed as Sharpa), and `/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. Each row is one
control step: wrist x/y/z targets in metres, wrist XYZ Euler joint targets in radians, then the finger targets in
`s.actuator_names` order. Do not save object
states as the deliverable: the verifier executes the actions from the frozen start in one fresh process.
NaN, infinity, object arrays and malformed or oversized trajectories are rejected.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Independent walnut rotation and selective release

Keep the wrist fixed. Turn walnut A +90 degrees around palm-local Y, return A to its initial orientation, then release only A into the catch tray. Maintain walnut B at its initial position and orientation throughout. The walnuts, standardized to the same maximum dimension, must never contact one another. Before selective release, keep both objects unsupported by the environment and in load-bearing hand contact. Finally let A settle in the tray while continuing to hold B. If walnut A drops toward the table (center below 0.135 m) or leaves the tray footprint (more than 0.10 m horizontally from the tray center), or walnut B slips, the episode fails immediately.

Palm-local axes belong to a frame fixed to the palm; with the wrist locked it is aligned with the world axes: +X points from the wrist toward the fingertips (world +x), +Y points across the palm from the thumb side toward the little-finger side (world +y), and +Z points out of the palm, which faces up (world +z). In the simulator it has the orientation of the `wrist_stage` body (the identity quaternion while the wrist is locked), not that of the palm link `right_hand_C_MC`, whose own axes are rotated relative to it. A turn about a palm-local axis is about that palm-fixed axis (it does not turn with the object), and a positive angle follows the right-hand rule: counterclockwise when seen from the positive end of the axis looking back toward the palm. So +90 degrees about Y carries the side of walnut A that faces up toward the fingertips.

You control one dexterous hand on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage: a Sharpa Wave hand with 22 independently
actuated finger joints (the default) or a Wuji Hand 2.2 with 20 (see Hands).
The wrist stage is position actuated in the physics engine; grasping and manipulating require physical contact.
The five fingers are thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

This is a fixed-wrist essential dexterity task. Native equality constraints lock all six wrist joints.
The first six entries of every action MUST remain [-0.08, 0, 0.29, 0, 0, 0].
Float32 wire-format rounding is accepted and normalized to those exact fixed targets before physics runs.
Use the declared target values rather than copying measured wrist joint positions. Only the finger targets may
change. Objects have no actuators, scripted motion or grasp attachments; they move through contact and normal gravity.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Sharpa rows: the six wrist targets, then `right_thumb_CMC_FE, right_thumb_CMC_AA, right_thumb_MCP_FE, right_thumb_MCP_AA, right_thumb_IP`, `right_<index|middle|ring>_MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP` and `right_pinky_CMC, _MCP_FE, _MCP_AA, _PIP, _DIP`. Wuji rows: the same six wrist targets, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` (thumb CMC flexion, CMC abduction, MCP, IP) and `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `MFJ0..3`, `RFJ0..3`, `LFJ0..3` (index, middle, ring, pinky: MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP). Both hands are mounted in the same wrist frame; Sharpa fingers use the dissipative velocity coefficient declared in the frozen instance, Wuji fingers the manufacturer's position servos. Sharpa starts from the instance's declared finger pose; Wuji starts from the pose in `wuji_reset.json` (neutral fingers when the file is absent), an authoring choice that keeps the object held at reset, not a policy. The wrist, fixtures and predicate are identical for both hands; where a Wuji grasp cannot hold an object at the Sharpa start pose, `wuji_reset.json` also declares the held objects' start poses in the Wuji grasp, and every reset-relative quantity is measured from the post-reset pose.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Success predicate
The verifier evaluates these conditions on features it computes from simulator state (values rounded to six significant digits here; the verifier uses the frozen task's unrounded values, which differ from these only beyond the sixth significant digit). A stage or the terminal condition counts a control sample only if its bounds held at every 2 ms physics substep of that control interval; stages are completed in order and each starts after the previous one.

1. Stage `rotate_a_keep_b`: `0 <= a_quarter_turn_error <= 0.16`, `1 <= a_finger_contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
   While this stage is active (fail-fast): `a_hand_contacts >= 1`, `a_support == 0`, `0 <= a_position_error <= 0.035`, `0 <= speed <= 12`.
2. Stage `return_a_keep_b`: `0 <= a_orientation_error <= 0.16`, `1 <= a_finger_contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.25`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
   While this stage is active (fail-fast): `a_hand_contacts >= 1`, `a_support == 0`, `0 <= a_position_error <= 0.035`, `0 <= speed <= 12`.
3. Stage `release_a_only`: `a_hand_contacts == 0`, `deposit_support_a >= 1`, `0 <= a_deposit_distance <= 0.04`, for 5 consecutive control samples.
   While this stage is active (fail-fast): `0 <= a_linear_speed <= 2.5`, `0 <= a_angular_speed <= 80`.
4. Terminal hold after the last stage: `a_hand_contacts == 0`, `deposit_support_a >= 1`, `0 <= a_deposit_distance <= 0.04`, `1 <= b_finger_contacts <= 5`, `0 <= speed <= 0.06`, for 25 consecutive control samples.

Invariants, checked at every physics substep for the whole episode (fail-fast): `0 <= force <= 80`, `0 <= palm_drift <= 0.003`, `0 <= wrist_rotation <= 0.01`, `ball_pair_contacts == 0`, `0 <= b_position_error <= 0.015`, `0 <= b_orientation_error <= 0.2`, `b_support == 0`, `b_hand_contacts >= 1`, `1 <= b_finger_contacts <= 5`, `0 <= a_linear_speed <= 2.5`, `0 <= a_angular_speed <= 80`, `0.135 <= a_height <= 0.6`, `0 <= a_deposit_distance <= 0.1`.

The first violated invariant or guard, a non-finite feature or unstable physics fails the episode immediately and permanently: the episode ends there and later rows are not executed, so a dropped, slipped or knocked-away object can never be recovered in that episode (a reset starts a new one: `## Episodes and resets`). Success is reached when the terminal hold completes; the episode ends there too. Completing only some stages is a failure.

Feature definitions:
- `a_quarter_turn_error`: rotation between walnut A and its +90 degree target about the declared axis, rad
- `a_finger_contacts`: fingers touching walnut A (> 0.005 N)
- `speed`: largest absolute velocity of any task-object degree of freedom, m/s or rad/s (peak over the substeps)
- `a_hand_contacts`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between walnut A and the hand
- `a_support`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between walnut A and the environment
- `a_position_error`: walnut A displacement from its reset position in the palm frame, m
- `a_orientation_error`: walnut A rotation from its reset orientation in the palm frame, rad
- `deposit_support_a`: contacts between walnut A and the catch-tray floor
- `a_deposit_distance`: horizontal distance of walnut A from the catch-tray centre, m
- `a_linear_speed`: walnut A linear speed, m/s
- `a_angular_speed`: walnut A angular speed, rad/s
- `b_finger_contacts`: fingers touching walnut B (> 0.005 N)
- `force`: largest contact force on any task object, N (peak over the 2 ms substeps)
- `palm_drift`: palm displacement from its reset position, m
- `wrist_rotation`: palm rotation from its reset orientation, rad
- `ball_pair_contacts`: contacts between the two walnuts
- `b_position_error`: walnut B displacement from its reset position in the palm frame, m
- `b_orientation_error`: walnut B rotation from its reset orientation in the palm frame, rad
- `b_support`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between walnut B and the environment
- `b_hand_contacts`: contacts (> 0.005 N) between walnut B and the hand
- `a_height`: height of walnut A's centre, m (the tray floor is at about 0.155 m, the table top at 0.10 m)

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for Sharpa or `(T, 26)`
for Wuji (at most 50,000 rows) and the `hand` it was made for, as written by `s.save_trajectory` (an archive
without `hand` is replayed as Sharpa), and `/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. Each row is one
control step: wrist x/y/z targets in metres, wrist XYZ Euler joint targets in radians, then the finger targets in
`s.actuator_names` order. Do not save object
states as the deliverable: the verifier executes the actions from the frozen start in one fresh process.
NaN, infinity, object arrays and malformed or oversized trajectories are rejected.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Install a desk fan front guard

Install the front guard on the desk fan. The unpowered fan stands on the worktop facing the operator (its axis points along world -x); its rear wire guard carries four perimeter U clips at 45, 135, 225 and 315 degrees. All four clips start swung open (hinge angle 1.40 rad); the hand has to close every one of them. A closed lower clip (225 or 315 degrees) forms an open-topped U channel that can carry the guard's rim. The detached front guard (0.369 m wire cage, 185 g, with a raised hub cap at its centre) lies flat on the worktop, dome up. Lift the guard, turn it upright with its dome facing the operator, seat its rim on the rear rim, close all four clips over the two rims (the lower clips may be closed before or after the guard is seated; the upper clips can only lock over a seated guard), and take the hand away. Success requires, in order: (1) the guard seated: guard centre within 5 mm of the fan axis, axial seat error within 2.5 mm and guard axis within 5 degrees of the fan axis; (2) the guard still seated, all four clip hinges in their locked range (hinge angle at most 0.12 rad) and the guard rim inside every clip's U channel (in each clip's frame, with origin at its hinge, x toward the operator along world -x and y radially outward, the guard-rim point nearest that clip lies at x from 6.8 to 9.9 mm for the upper clips and 6.8 to 8.6 mm for the lower clips and y from -4.8 to -2.2 mm, i.e. between the rear rim and the clip's lip and inside its bridge), each upper clip having locked at or after the first control at which the guard was seated; (3) the complete condition with no hand contact on the guard, the clips or the fan, guard speed at most 0.02 m/s and angular speed at most 0.2 rad/s, for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; a guard that is only placed, or clips that are only partly closed, never count. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when the fan moves more than 3 cm from its start or tilts more than 0.10 rad, when the guard touches the worktop, a table leg or the floor after its centre of mass has been lifted more than 5 cm above its resting height (dropped or set back down), or at the first substep at which the guard touches nothing while its centre of mass falls faster than 0.2 m/s (dropped, even if caught again), when the guard touches the fan's base, stem, neck, motor housing, feet or buttons, when the guard's centre of mass falls below the worktop (z < 0.65 m) or leaves the workspace box x in [0.20, 1.10] m, y in [-0.55, 0.55] m, z in [0.60, 1.40] m, or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed; no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. The clips are rigid U channels on passive hinges held by an elastic over-centre spring (a modelled snap detent); the guard is a rigid wire cage. The episode allows at most 6000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.

You control one dexterous hand mounted on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three serial revolute
joints, no arm). The stage and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under native force bounds;
grasping, carrying and releasing require physical contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics
substeps.

## Scene facts (world frame, metres and radians, z up)
- Worktop: top at z = 0.65, spanning x in [0.28, 1.08], y in [-0.50, 0.50].
- Fan (free body on four rubber feet, 2.15 kg with its clips): body frame starts at (0.73, 0.18, 0.952) with the cage
  axis along world -x. The rear rim (radius 0.1845, wire radius 0.0018) lies in the plane x = 0.73.
- Clip hinges (fixed to the fan; hinge axis tangential to the rim; angle 0 closed over both rims, 1.40 open, the
  elastic detent's over-centre point at 0.70): 45 deg (0.734, 0.3128, 1.0848), 135 deg (0.734, 0.0472, 1.0848),
  225 deg (0.734, 0.0472, 0.8192), 315 deg (0.734, 0.3128, 0.8192). All four clips start open at 1.40 (as in the source
  scene). A closed lower clip (225 or 315 deg) forms an open-topped U channel that can carry the guard's rim; an upper
  clip only counts when it locks at or after the first seated control.
- Front guard (rigid, 0.185 kg): rim radius 0.1845 (wire radius 0.0018), dish 0.047 deep toward the operator, a hub
  cap of radius 0.043 and height 0.022 at its centre (front face 0.057 in front of the rim plane), centre of mass
  0.018 in front of the rim plane on the axis. It starts flat on the worktop, dome up, rim centre at
  (0.48, -0.275, 0.6518).
- Seat: the guard is seated with its centre at (0.72635, 0.18, 0.952), i.e. 3.65 mm in front of the rear-rim plane,
  axis along world -x; the stage-1 tolerances in the task text are measured from this pose in the fan's frame.
- Wrist stage: targets are world positions x in [-0.2, 1.0], y in [-0.6, 0.6], z in [0.35, 1.55] and serial XYZ
  angles in [-3.14, 3.14]; it starts at (0.40, 0.00, 0.95, 3.0, 0, 0) (palm down, fingers along +x).
- Cameras (640 x 480): `overview` at (-0.06, -0.84, 1.40) looking at (0.60, -0.07, 0.84), fovy 45; `closeup` at
  (0.20, -0.27, 1.22) looking at (0.72, 0.17, 1.00), fovy 55.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Both hands hang from the same six-axis wrist stage, with the same wrist joints, ranges, gains and start targets.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

## Hands

Both hands hang from the same six-axis wrist stage, with the same wrist joints, ranges, gains and start targets.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `28` wide for `sharpa` and `26` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control. The first six entries are the wrist-stage targets, identical for both hands:
`wrist_x, wrist_y, wrist_z` (metres, world frame) and `wrist_rx, wrist_ry, wrist_rz` (radians, serial XYZ joints, not a
quaternion). The finger targets follow in native actuator order, in radians:

- `sharpa`: 28 values, the six wrist targets and 22 Sharpa Wave finger targets `right_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `right_pinky_DIP`.
- `wuji`: 26 values, the same six wrist targets and 20 Wuji Hand 2.2 finger targets `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3`,
  `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_MFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_RFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_LFJ0..3`.

Every target must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`. Both hands start from the same wrist targets; the frozen
finger start pose of each hand is in `task.json` (`initial_targets`).

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 26)`
for `wuji`, at most 6000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

DexHand: Operate a manual coffee grinder

dexhand-grinder-crank-i00 · upstream folder tasks/dexhand/dexhand-grinder-crank-i00-standard

With a fixed dual-arm robot (Tianji Marvin, a dexterous hand on each arm: two Sharpa Wave hands by default, or two Wuji Hand 2.2), counterhold a free-standing manual coffee grinder with one hand and turn its passive, friction-loaded crank two full turns clockwise by the knob with the other, then let go and leave it standing; tipping, sliding, spinning or reversing the crank fails at once.
  • Original environment (the task's own code in its Docker image, MuJoCo 3.4.0), packaged reference actions, control rows counted from 0: Sharpa Wave: success after 996 controls (stages reached at control rows 809 and 995). The start-state hash equals the one frozen in the task, in MuJoCo 3.4.0 and in 3.8.0. The scene text this machine builds differs from the image's in the last digits of 2 of 32495 numbers (its builder computes them with numpy); the original code under MuJoCo 3.8.0 was therefore handed the image's text, the design's shim (c).
  • Same engine (the original's own engine, MuJoCo 3.4.0): the exported scene file, stepped by the port's own loop, gives exactly the bits of the original code: the full simulation state after every one of 4,454 controls, over the reference and 5 perturbed copies of it, for Sharpa Wave.
  • Same engine (our engine, MuJoCo 3.8.0): the exported scene file, stepped by the port's own loop, gives exactly the bits of the original code: the full simulation state after every one of 4,452 controls, over the reference and 5 perturbed copies of it, for Sharpa Wave.
  • The ported success rule (the original checker with only its robot look-ups replaced) gives the same stage, hold counter, success flag, failure name and all 28 feature values as the original checker after every control of those runs, in both engines. The perturbed rows end in grinder_slid and grinder_tipped, so 2 of the rule's 9 failure conditions were exercised (including the runs on the translated text); the others were not triggered by any row set.
  • The two engines compile the exported file to the same model: 423 of 433 numeric arrays are identical (masses, inertias, geometry, friction, solver and actuator parameters); the 10 that differ are mesh polygon and normal tables and storage offsets, which each engine builds for itself, and every option flag is equal by name for the exported text (the text with the declared translations differs from the original engine only in the declared flag invdiscrete).
  • The same actions across the two engines, file as exported: Sharpa Wave: robot joints agree to 2.2e-16 until a servo first sits on its force limit (control row 53) and differ by up to 4.6e-03 before the robot first touches the scene (control row 95), the objects differ by 2.7e-17 after the first control, by more than 1e-6 after 96 controls and by more than 1e-3 after 103 controls (largest difference over the 994 controls both runs executed: 1.5e-02 for robot joints, 5.4e-01 for the objects). Outcome of the references in our engine: Sharpa Wave: success after 994 controls (stages reached at control rows 810 and 993).
  • With the declared engine translations (<flag invdiscrete="enable"> written into <option>; invdiscrete is MuJoCo's documented opt-out of the free-body midpoint integration it added in 3.7.0): Sharpa Wave: robot joints agree to 2.2e-16 until a servo first sits on its force limit (control row 53) and differ by up to 4.6e-03 before the robot first touches the scene (control row 95), the objects differ by 2.7e-17 after the first control, by more than 1e-6 after 96 controls and by more than 1e-3 after 103 controls (largest difference over the 994 controls both runs executed: 1.5e-02 for robot joints, 5.4e-01 for the objects). Outcome of the references: Sharpa Wave: success after 994 controls (stages reached at control rows 810 and 993).
  • The translated text is inert in the original engine: with the added flags MuJoCo 3.4.0 still reproduces the original recording bit for bit on every row set.
  • Yardstick, inside the original engine alone (MuJoCo 3.4.0 against itself, the reference replayed after moving one object's start by 1e-12; it shows how much of a difference is the reference's own sensitivity): Sharpa Wave: with the start of grinder_free moved by 1e-12 the objects differ from the unmoved run by more than 1e-6 after 869 controls and never by more than 1e-3; between the two engines the same thresholds are passed after 96 controls and 103 controls. Counting the unmoved replay and the moved ones (in ours: as exported and with the translations): Sharpa Wave: the reference succeeds in 2 of 2 runs in the original engine and in 4 of 4 in ours (2 of 2 as exported, 2 of 2 with the translations): the same outcome in both engines.
  • One control (20 ms) stepped from the original's own recorded states, warm start included: Sharpa Wave: exactly zero on 996 of 996 controls in 3.4.0; in 3.8.0 as exported the median error is 6.0e-10 for robot joints and 1.3e-09 for the objects (largest 1.3e-03); with the translations the median is 6.0e-10 and 1.3e-09, the 99th percentile 5.2e-04 and 2.4e-08, the largest 1.3e-03 (engine gap within the measured range).
  • A further difference between the engines that needs no contact: a position servo sitting on its force limit is advanced differently by MuJoCo 3.4.0 and 3.8.0. Same one-control test: Sharpa Wave: in the 140 controls in which the robot touches nothing and no servo is on its force limit the robot's error is at most 1.1e-16; in the 10 controls in which a servo is on its force limit and the robot still touches nothing it reaches 1.3e-03. No setting was changed.
  • Its cause is documented by MuJoCo: the changelog of version 3.5.0 (12 February 2026), bug fix 24, says that in the implicit integrators' derivatives 'actuator velocity derivatives were incorrectly computed when the force was clamped by forcerange'. The original runs on MuJoCo 3.4.0, before that fix, and we run 3.8.0, after it. A single hinge with the arm's servo gains agrees (one 2 ms step from 0.5 rad/s, implicitfast): with the servo on its 18 N m force limit through the actuator's forcerange MuJoCo 3.4.0 gives 0.532847 rad/s, the step with the velocity gain of the servo in the implicit matrix, and MuJoCo 3.8.0 gives 0.536000 rad/s, the step without the velocity gain; far from the limit they give 0.468978 and 0.468978 rad/s.
  • It concerns the original robot's own servos, which our rig replaces: Sharpa Wave: all 14 actuators of the model that have a force limit belong to the original robot, and the ones on their limit when those controls begin are 2 servos of its left arm (found at the start of 10 of those 10 controls). The difference therefore gets no engine translation in the port (the original robot is not part of it); it is reported.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Operate a manual coffee grinder

Operate the manual coffee grinder on the counter with the two hands of the dual-arm robot standing at the counter. The HARIO-style hand mill (0.40 kg, 174 mm body, 26 mm base radius) stands free on the counter top (z = 0.70 m) with its base centre at (0.45, 0, 0.70) m. Its crank turns on a passive hinge about the grinder axis with grinding resistance (0.08 N m dry friction and 0.012 N m s/rad damping); the knob sits on a free spin bearing at 80 mm crank radius. The grinder is light and narrow: it tips over if the crank is driven without holding the body. Hold the grinder body with one hand and turn the crank by its knob with the other until the crank has turned at least two full turns (720 degrees) net clockwise as seen from above, measured as the unwrapped crank hinge angle relative to the grinder body. Then let go of the grinder. Success requires, at the same time: the crank still at least 720 degrees net clockwise, no contact between any part of either hand and any part of the grinder (body, crank or knob), the grinder base resting on the counter, the grinder axis within 10 degrees of vertical, grinder centre-of-mass linear speed at most 0.02 m/s, grinder angular speed at most 0.2 rad/s and crank speed at most 0.5 rad/s; this complete condition must hold for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; turning the crank without the released hold never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when the grinder axis tilts more than 10 degrees from vertical, the grinder base moves more than 2 cm horizontally from its start or rises more than 2 cm, the base falls below the counter top (z < 0.695 m), the grinder body turns more than 45 degrees about its own axis, the crank has turned more than 90 degrees net counter-clockwise, an arm, torso or stand link of the robot touches anything (only the hands may make contact), or the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only the robot's actuator targets (14 arm joints and the fingers of both hands) are allowed: no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct forces on the grinder. Grinding itself is summarised by the crank angle; no beans or grounds are simulated. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.

You control a fixed dual-arm robot (Tianji Marvin: two 7-joint arms on a stand) with a dexterous hand of the same model on each
wrist: a right hand and a left hand. The arm joints and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under
native force bounds; holding the grinder and turning the crank require physical contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz,
with ten 2 ms physics substeps. The stand faces +x behind the counter on the floor (z = -0.1 m), its base origin at
(-0.085, 0, 0) m (shoulders 1.121 m above it, at y = +-0.2215 m); any contact of an arm, torso or stand link with
anything ends the episode (`robot_collision`).

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Each row starts with the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (left arm J1-J7, then right arm J1-J7, radians), followed by the left hand's finger targets and then the right hand's (22 per hand for `sharpa`: the genuine right Sharpa Wave on the right flange and its declared mirror image on the left flange; 20 per hand for `wuji`). The left hand counterholds the grinder, the right hand turns the crank.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`58` for `sharpa`, `54` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).
Full task description (original text, privileged setting; differs from the standard one)
# DexHand: Operate a manual coffee grinder

Operate the manual coffee grinder on the counter with the two hands of the dual-arm robot standing at the counter. The HARIO-style hand mill (0.40 kg, 174 mm body, 26 mm base radius) stands free on the counter top (z = 0.70 m) with its base centre at (0.45, 0, 0.70) m. Its crank turns on a passive hinge about the grinder axis with grinding resistance (0.08 N m dry friction and 0.012 N m s/rad damping); the knob sits on a free spin bearing at 80 mm crank radius. The grinder is light and narrow: it tips over if the crank is driven without holding the body. Hold the grinder body with one hand and turn the crank by its knob with the other until the crank has turned at least two full turns (720 degrees) net clockwise as seen from above, measured as the unwrapped crank hinge angle relative to the grinder body. Then let go of the grinder. Success requires, at the same time: the crank still at least 720 degrees net clockwise, no contact between any part of either hand and any part of the grinder (body, crank or knob), the grinder base resting on the counter, the grinder axis within 10 degrees of vertical, grinder centre-of-mass linear speed at most 0.02 m/s, grinder angular speed at most 0.2 rad/s and crank speed at most 0.5 rad/s; this complete condition must hold for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; turning the crank without the released hold never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when the grinder axis tilts more than 10 degrees from vertical, the grinder base moves more than 2 cm horizontally from its start or rises more than 2 cm, the base falls below the counter top (z < 0.695 m), the grinder body turns more than 45 degrees about its own axis, the crank has turned more than 90 degrees net counter-clockwise, an arm, torso or stand link of the robot touches anything (only the hands may make contact), or the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only the robot's actuator targets (14 arm joints and the fingers of both hands) are allowed: no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct forces on the grinder. Grinding itself is summarised by the crank angle; no beans or grounds are simulated. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.

You control a fixed dual-arm robot (Tianji Marvin: two 7-joint arms on a stand) with a dexterous hand of the same model on each
wrist: a right hand and a left hand. The arm joints and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under
native force bounds; holding the grinder and turning the crank require physical contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz,
with ten 2 ms physics substeps. The stand faces +x behind the counter on the floor (z = -0.1 m), its base origin at
(-0.085, 0, 0) m (shoulders 1.121 m above it, at y = +-0.2215 m); any contact of an arm, torso or stand link with
anything ends the episode (`robot_collision`).

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Each row starts with the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (left arm J1-J7, then right arm J1-J7, radians), followed by the left hand's finger targets and then the right hand's (22 per hand for `sharpa`: the genuine right Sharpa Wave on the right flange and its declared mirror image on the left flange; 20 per hand for `wuji`). The left hand counterholds the grinder, the right hand turns the crank.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `58` wide for `sharpa` and `54` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control: the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (radians) `SHOULDER_PITCH_L_J1_target,
SHOULDER_ROLL_L_J2_target, ELBOW_PITCH_L_J3_target, ELBOW_YAW_L_J4_target, WRIST_PITCH_L_J5_target,
WRIST_YAW_L_J6_target, WRIST_ROLL_L_J7_target`, then the same seven for the right arm (`..._R_J1_target` ...
`..._R_J7_target`), then the finger targets in native actuator order, in radians, left hand first:

- `sharpa`: 58 values, the 14 arm targets, 22 left Sharpa Wave finger targets `left_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `left_pinky_DIP`,
  then 22 right targets `right_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `right_pinky_DIP`. The left Sharpa Wave is the right model reflected
  in y.
- `wuji`: 54 values, the same 14 arm targets, 20 left Wuji Hand 2.2 targets `l_wuji_l_THJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_FFJ0..3`,
  `l_wuji_l_MFJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_RFJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_LFJ0..3`, then the manufacturer's right hand `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3` ...
  `r_wuji_r_LFJ0..3`.

Arm servos: kp 700 N m/rad, kv 48 N m s/rad, force limits 108 / 108 / 66 / 66 / 18 / 18 / 18 N m (J1 ... J7), no
gravity compensation. Each hand sits rigidly on its arm's flange (bodies `right_wrist_stage` / `left_wrist_stage`:
fingers along the flange +z, palm normal +x, thumb +y for the right hand). No IK primitive is supplied. Every target
must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`; the frozen start pose (arm joints; open fingers) is in `task.json`
(`initial_targets`).

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 58)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 54)`
for `wuji`, at most 3000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Open a jam jar and set the lid aside

Open the jam jar with the robot's right hand and set its lid aside on the worktop. Scene (world frame, metres, z up, +x forward from the robot): the worktop top is at z = 0.75 and spans |x| <= 0.45, |y| <= 0.58. A filled 297 ml glass jam jar (550 g, 67 mm body diameter, 110 mm tall, rim at z = 0.86) stands upright on the worktop centred at x = -0.22, y = -0.08. Nothing holds the jar: it stands on its own weight and glass-on-worktop friction, which resists only about 0.13 N m of twisting torque, so the hand must turn the lid without turning, sliding or tipping the jar. Its red 64.8 mm twist-off steel lid (32 g) is closed. Jar and lid are free rigid bodies. The closure is a lug thread made of contact geometry only: four inclined glass ramps on the jar neck hold four inward lugs of the lid, so the closed lid cannot be pulled off. Turning the lid counter-clockwise seen from above (positive rotation about +z relative to the jar) slides the lugs up the ramps; at 1.049 rad they pass the ramp ends, and while they sit in the gaps between the ramps (turn between 1.049 and about 1.26 rad) the lid lifts off freely; turned further without lifting, the lugs run into the next ramps' leads, and turning clockwise from the closed position tightens and jams. The lid is lightly closed: no vacuum, seal adhesion or tightening torque is modelled, and the jam is part of the jar's rigid mass, not a fluid. Complete three stages in this order. (1) Unscrew: while the lid is still seated on the thread (lid origin less than 6 mm above its closed height and within 4 mm of the jar axis, in the jar frame), its counter-clockwise turn relative to the jar, unwrapped after every physics substep, reaches at least 1.049 rad. (2) Lift clear: afterwards, the lowest point of the lid skirt rises more than 30 mm above the jar rim. (3) Set aside: afterwards, for 50 consecutive controls (1 s), the lid touches the worktop and touches neither the hand nor the jar, is upright (tilt at most 0.15 rad), has its centre at least 90 mm horizontally from the jar axis, moves at most 0.02 m/s and turns at most 0.3 rad/s, while the jar touches the worktop, is not touched by the hand, is upright within 0.10 rad and moves at most 0.02 m/s. The episode ends with success at that moment; a partial sequence never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when: the jar tilts more than 15 degrees (jar_tipped), slides more than 30 mm horizontally from its start (jar_slid) or is lifted more than 15 mm (jar_lifted); the lid touches the worktop before stage 2 (lid_knocked_off); the lid drops: while it is in the air (its lowest point more than 10 mm above the worktop top), at any substep it touches nothing (no hand, jar or worktop contact) while its centre of mass moves downward faster than 0.3 m/s (about a 5 mm free fall; there is no window to catch it again), or its centre of mass moves downward faster than 1.0 m/s whatever it touches (lid_dropped); a lid that tips over or falls flat on the worktop (lowest point within 10 mm of the worktop top) has not dropped; the jar or the lid touches the floor, its origin falls more than 5 mm below the worktop top or leaves the worktop footprint (lid_off_table, jar_off_table) or the workspace box x in [-0.45, 0.45] m, y in [-0.40, 0.40] m, z in [0.73, 1.25] m (object_left_workspace); the lid leaves the thread upward while its lugs are not in the gaps between the ramps, i.e. its turn modulo pi/2 is outside [1.019, 1.291] rad (lid_forced_through_thread); the parked left arm or the left hand touches the jar or the lid (left_arm_contact; moving the left arm is not blocked, but the task is done by the right arm and hand); or the physics becomes unstable (unstable_physics). Later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed: the joints of the Marvin right arm and its hand (the left arm stays parked with its hand open), no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. Any robot part touching the jar or the lid counts as the hand touching it. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.

You control the right arm and right hand of a fixed Tianji Marvin robot: a stand with two 7-joint arms and a dexterous
hand on each wrist (the robot stands behind the worktop, its base centre at x = -0.56, y = 0.08 on the floor, facing
+x; shoulders at z = 1.121 m (1.221 m above the floor)). The left arm stays parked beside the torso with its hand open; the task is done
by the right arm and hand alone. Every arm and finger joint is a position servo inside the physics engine under native
force bounds; arm servos have stiffness 700 N m/rad, damping 48 N m s/rad and **no gravity compensation** (a held
target sags under the arm's weight unless your targets account for it). Turning, lifting, carrying and releasing the
lid require physical contact, and the jar is held by nothing but its own weight and friction on the worktop. The
controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps. At reset the right hand hangs open, palm down, about 0.1 m
above the lid with its fingers along +x; the left arm is at its parked pose.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Each row starts with the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (left arm J1-J7, then right arm J1-J7), followed by the left hand's finger targets and then the right hand's (22 per hand for `sharpa`, 20 per hand for `wuji`); the left arm is parked and only the right arm/hand perform the task.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`58` for `sharpa`, `54` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

You control the right arm and right hand of a fixed Tianji Marvin robot: a stand with two 7-joint arms and a dexterous
hand on each wrist (the robot stands behind the worktop, its base centre at x = -0.56, y = 0.08 on the floor, facing

force bounds; arm servos have stiffness 700 N m/rad, damping 48 N m s/rad and **no gravity compensation** (a held

lid require physical contact, and the jar is held by nothing but its own weight and friction on the worktop. The
controller runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps. At reset the right hand hangs open, palm down, about 0.1 m
above the lid with its fingers along +x; the left arm is at its parked pose.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Each row starts with the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (left arm J1-J7, then right arm J1-J7), followed by the left hand's finger targets and then the right hand's (22 per hand for `sharpa`, 20 per hand for `wuji`); the left arm is parked and only the right arm/hand perform the task.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `58` wide for `sharpa` and `54` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control and holds a position target for every actuator, in radians:

- `sharpa` (58 values): 0-6 the left arm `SHOULDER_PITCH_L_J1, SHOULDER_ROLL_L_J2, ELBOW_PITCH_L_J3, ELBOW_YAW_L_J4,
  WRIST_PITCH_L_J5, WRIST_YAW_L_J6, WRIST_ROLL_L_J7` (actuators `<joint>_target`; keep them at the parked start
  values), 7-13 the same right-arm joints (`..._R_J1` to `..._R_J7`), 14-35 the 22 left Sharpa Wave finger targets
  `left_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `left_pinky_DIP`, 36-57 the 22 right Sharpa Wave finger targets `right_thumb_CMC_FE` ...
  `right_pinky_DIP`.
- `wuji` (54 values): 0-13 the same arm targets, 14-33 the 20 left Wuji Hand 2.2 finger targets `l_wuji_l_THJ0..3`,
  `l_wuji_l_FFJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_MFJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_RFJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_LFJ0..3`, 34-53 the 20 right ones
  (`r_wuji_r_...`, same order).

Every target must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`. The frozen start targets of each hand are in `task.json`
(`initial_targets`); the right hand's frame is the body `wrist_stage` on the right flange (fingers along its +z, palm
normal +x, thumb +y), which forward kinematics of the arm joints places in the world.

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 58)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 54)`
for `wuji`, at most 3000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.
