Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Assemble a wooden stool cross brace

Assemble the cross brace of a pine stool dry frame. The lower side frame lies flat on the table with its four bores facing up and three rails already standing seated in three of them. The loose cross brace (a 0.26 m pine rail with an 8 mm dowel exposed 15 mm at each end) lies on the table, and the opposite side frame lies upside down beside the lower frame. Pick up the brace, seat one of its dowels in the empty bore of the lower frame, then lift the opposite side frame and lower it onto all four upper dowels so that both brace dowels end up seated in their legs. Ordered stages: (1) brace lifted: no brace-table contact, brace centre raised at least 0.05 m and its lowest bounding-box corner at least 0.02 m above the table top; (2) one brace dowel seated in a lower-frame bore; (3) opposite side frame lifted (the same lift test); (4) assembled: each of the eight bores holds exactly one seated dowel and every rail, the brace included, has one dowel seated in each side frame. A dowel is seated in a bore when its tip is 12 mm to 19 mm past the bore entry along the bore axis (12 mm is 80% of the exposed dowel), its tip is within 1.6 mm of the bore axis and the dowel axis is within 0.105 rad of the bore axis. Success: after stage 4 the assembled condition holds with no hand contact on any frame or rail and every part's centre-of-mass speed at most 0.02 m/s and angular speed at most 0.2 rad/s for 50 consecutive controls (1 s); the episode then ends. A single seated brace dowel or any partial assembly never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when the lower frame moves more than 0.03 m or tilts more than 10 degrees; a pre-seated rail is pulled to less than 8 mm in its bore or tilts more than 10 degrees; the brace touches the table after stage 1, or its centre drops below 0.09 m above the table top after stage 1; the brace tilts more than 20 degrees after stage 2; the opposite side frame touches the table after stage 3 or tilts more than 20 degrees from its upside-down carrying orientation after stage 3; any part with no contact at all (not held, not supported) has its centre of mass falling faster than 0.2 m/s (a drop); any part touches the floor, has its centre below the table top (z < 0.74 m) or leaves the workspace box x in [0.23, 1.23] m, y in [-0.73, 1.03] m, z in [0.70, 1.60] m; or the physics becomes unstable. Later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed: no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. All parts are free rigid pine bodies; the bores are hollow contact geometry of the source size (4.1 mm radius for the 4.0 mm dowels: 0.1 mm radial clearance, no entry chamfer); glue, screws, the seat and load capacity are not modelled. The episode allows at most 6000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.

You control one dexterous hand mounted on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three serial revolute
joints, no arm). The stage and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under native force bounds;
grasping, carrying, inserting and releasing require physical contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with
ten 2 ms physics substeps.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Both hands hang from the same six-axis wrist stage, with the same wrist joints, ranges, gains and start targets; the wrist x/y/z targets are offsets from the stage origin (stage origin (0.55, -0.1, 1.15) m) along the world axes, and at zero wrist angles the palm faces down with the fingers along +x.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`28` for `sharpa`, `26` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

Later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed: no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. All parts are free rigid pine bodies; the bores are hollow contact geometry of the source size (4.1 mm radius for the 4.0 mm dowels: 0.1 mm radial clearance, no entry chamfer); glue, screws, the seat and load capacity are not modelled. You control one dexterous hand mounted on a six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three serial revolute
joints, no arm). The stage and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under native force bounds;
grasping, carrying, inserting and releasing require physical contact. The controller runs at 50 Hz, with
ten 2 ms physics substeps.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Both hands hang from the same six-axis wrist stage, with the same wrist joints, ranges, gains and start targets; the wrist x/y/z targets are offsets from the stage origin (stage origin (0.55, -0.1, 1.15) m) along the world axes, and at zero wrist angles the palm faces down with the fingers along +x.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `28` wide for `sharpa` and `26` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control. The first six entries are the wrist-stage targets, identical for both hands:
`wrist_x, wrist_y, wrist_z` (metres, offsets of the stage from its origin `task.json` `stage_origin`, along the world
axes) and `wrist_rx, wrist_ry, wrist_rz` (radians, serial XYZ joints, not a quaternion). At zero wrist angles the palm
faces down, the fingers point along +x and the thumb is on the +y side. The finger targets follow in native actuator
order, in radians:

- `sharpa`: 28 values, the six wrist targets and 22 Sharpa Wave finger targets `right_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `right_pinky_DIP`.
- `wuji`: 26 values, the same six wrist targets and 20 Wuji Hand 2.2 finger targets `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3`,
  `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_MFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_RFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_LFJ0..3`.

Every target must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`. Both hands start from the same wrist targets; the frozen
finger start pose of each hand is in `task.json` (`initial_targets`).

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 28)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 26)`
for `wuji`, at most 6000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Sweep debris into a held dustpan

Sweep all six pieces of debris on the floor into the dustpan and lift the loaded pan. A fixed two-arm robot starts with a broom held in its right hand and a dustpan held in its left hand; the pan's entrance ramp rests on the floor next to six small rigid debris pieces (packaging pieces, bottle caps, a wood chip and a crumpled-paper ball). Push the debris over the ramp with the broom's bristles, then raise the dustpan. Success requires 2000 consecutive physics steps (1.0 s) in which all of these hold: in the dustpan's own frame every collision shape of all six pieces lies over the pan floor (at least 1 mm inside its 460 mm side-to-side width, inside its 262 mm depth, no lower than 1 mm below the top of the floor plate and no higher than 110 mm above the pan origin); all six pieces touch the pan (contact force at least 1 mN); the pan origin is at least 50 mm above the floor; every piece moves slower than 0.03 m/s and rotates slower than 0.8 rad/s; and every piece has been touched by the bristles at some point. The episode ends with that success, or fails immediately and permanently when: a piece leaves the floor work area (world x outside [0.45, 1.00] m, y outside [-0.50, 0.40] m, or its center more than 0.25 m above or 0.01 m below the floor at z = -0.10 m); any part of the robot touches a piece of debris with at least 1 mN (sweep with the broom only); from 1.2 s on, fewer than two collision parts of a tool's own hand press on its handle with at least 0.01 N each, or the handle's grip point has moved more than 25 mm or turned more than 0.25 rad relative to that palm since 1.2 s (dropped or slipping tool); a tool is pressed (more than 0.01 N) by any robot part other than its own hand; the arms, torso or the two hands collide with each other; or the simulation becomes unstable. Five of six pieces, an unlifted pan or a hold shorter than 1 s is not a success. Only the robot's motor targets act; the tools and the debris are free bodies without welds, scripted motion or applied forces. One control row sets every motor target for one 0.5 ms physics step (2000 Hz); an episode has at most 160000 rows (80 s).

The robot is a fixed Tianji Marvin base with two seven-joint arms. The left arm's hand holds the dustpan by its
handle; the right arm's hand holds the broom by its shaft. Arms and fingers are position servos with native force
bounds; the broom, the dustpan and the debris move only through contact and gravity. At the start the current targets
keep both tools in the hands; the first 1.2 s are a settling period in which the grip is not yet judged. The simulator
integrates at 0.5 ms and every action row is one physics step, so rows are a 2000 Hz control. The service simulates
slower than real time (several seconds of CPU per simulated second).

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
This task uses two hands of one model on the two arms of a fixed robot: Sharpa Wave (default) or Wuji Hand 2.2. Every row holds both arms' joint targets and both hands' finger targets (layout below). With Wuji, both hands start closed on the same broom and dustpan (assets/reset_wuji.npz: the frozen arm, tool, debris and bristle coordinates with Wuji finger joints).
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`58` for `sharpa`, `54` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

Sharpa rows
(58 targets): the 7 left-arm joints `SHOULDER_PITCH_L_J1_target ... WRIST_ROLL_L_J7_target`, the 7 right-arm joints
`SHOULDER_PITCH_R_J1_target ... WRIST_ROLL_R_J7_target` (radians), then the 22 left-hand and the 22 right-hand
Sharpa Wave finger targets (radians).
Wuji rows (54 targets): the same 14 arm targets, then the 20 left-hand and the 20 right-hand Wuji Hand 2.2
finger targets (`l_wuji_l_THJ0 ... l_wuji_l_LFJ3`, `r_wuji_r_THJ0 ... r_wuji_r_LFJ3`: thumb CMC flexion, CMC
abduction, MCP, IP, then index/middle/ring/pinky MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP; radians). With Wuji the start
differs only in the finger joints and their targets: both Wuji hands start closed on the same broom and dustpan
(the arm, tool, debris and bristle coordinates and the arm targets are those of the Sharpa start), and
the targets at the start keep them. The task, predicate and fail-fast rules are the same for both hands.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).
Full task description (original text, privileged setting; differs from the standard one)
# DexHand: Sweep debris into a held dustpan

Sweep all six pieces of debris on the floor into the dustpan and lift the loaded pan. A fixed two-arm robot starts with a broom held in its right hand and a dustpan held in its left hand; the pan's entrance ramp rests on the floor next to six small rigid debris pieces (packaging pieces, bottle caps, a wood chip and a crumpled-paper ball). Push the debris over the ramp with the broom's bristles, then raise the dustpan. Success requires 2000 consecutive physics steps (1.0 s) in which all of these hold: in the dustpan's own frame every collision shape of all six pieces lies over the pan floor (at least 1 mm inside its 460 mm side-to-side width, inside its 262 mm depth, no lower than 1 mm below the top of the floor plate and no higher than 110 mm above the pan origin); all six pieces touch the pan (contact force at least 1 mN); the pan origin is at least 50 mm above the floor; every piece moves slower than 0.03 m/s and rotates slower than 0.8 rad/s; and every piece has been touched by the bristles at some point. The episode ends with that success, or fails immediately and permanently when: a piece leaves the floor work area (world x outside [0.45, 1.00] m, y outside [-0.50, 0.40] m, or its center more than 0.25 m above or 0.01 m below the floor at z = -0.10 m); any part of the robot touches a piece of debris with at least 1 mN (sweep with the broom only); from 1.2 s on, fewer than two collision parts of a tool's own hand press on its handle with at least 0.01 N each, or the handle's grip point has moved more than 25 mm or turned more than 0.25 rad relative to that palm since 1.2 s (dropped or slipping tool); a tool is pressed (more than 0.01 N) by any robot part other than its own hand; the arms, torso or the two hands collide with each other; or the simulation becomes unstable. Five of six pieces, an unlifted pan or a hold shorter than 1 s is not a success. Only the robot's motor targets act; the tools and the debris are free bodies without welds, scripted motion or applied forces. One control row sets every motor target for one 0.5 ms physics step (2000 Hz); an episode has at most 160000 rows (80 s).

The robot is a fixed Tianji Marvin base with two seven-joint arms. The left arm's hand holds the dustpan by its
handle; the right arm's hand holds the broom by its shaft. Arms and fingers are position servos with native force
bounds; the broom, the dustpan and the debris move only through contact and gravity. At the reset the motor targets
(`s.hold_action()`) keep both tools in the hands; the first 1.2 s are a settling period in which the grip is not yet
judged. MuJoCo 3.4.0 integrates at 0.5 ms (implicitfast, elliptic friction cones), and every control row is applied
for exactly one physics step, so a row is a 2000 Hz control. Simulating one second of this scene costs a few seconds
of CPU: plan with `snapshot()`/`restore()` instead of replaying from the start. Save a
deliverable early and improve it.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
This task uses two hands of one model on the two arms of a fixed robot: Sharpa Wave (default) or Wuji Hand 2.2. Every row holds both arms' joint targets and both hands' finger targets (layout below). With Wuji, both hands start closed on the same broom and dustpan (assets/reset_wuji.npz: the frozen arm, tool, debris and bristle coordinates with Wuji finger joints).
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `58` wide for `sharpa` and `54` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

Sharpa rows (58 targets): the 7 left-arm joints
`SHOULDER_PITCH_L_J1_target ... WRIST_ROLL_L_J7_target`, the 7 right-arm joints `SHOULDER_PITCH_R_J1_target ...
WRIST_ROLL_R_J7_target` (radians), then the 22 left-hand and the 22 right-hand Sharpa Wave finger targets
(`l_hand_thumb_CMC_FE ... l_hand_pinky_DIP`, `r_hand_thumb_CMC_FE ... r_hand_pinky_DIP`, radians).
Wuji rows (54 targets): the same 14 arm targets, then the 20 left-hand and the 20 right-hand Wuji Hand 2.2
finger targets (`l_wuji_l_THJ0 ... l_wuji_l_LFJ3`, `r_wuji_r_THJ0 ... r_wuji_r_LFJ3`: thumb CMC flexion, CMC
abduction, MCP, IP, then index/middle/ring/pinky MCP flexion, MCP abduction, PIP, DIP; radians). With Wuji the start
differs only in the finger joints and their targets: both Wuji hands start closed on the same broom and dustpan
(the arm, tool, debris and bristle coordinates and the arm targets are those of the Sharpa start), and
`s.hold_action()` keeps them. The task, predicate and fail-fast rules are the same for both hands.
The verifier rebuilds the scene with the archive's `hand` and rejects rows whose width does not match it.

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 58)` (Sharpa) or `(T, 54)`
(Wuji), 1 <= T <= 160000,
as a compressed archive of at most 64 MB, and `/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. Use `s.save_trajectory(actions, "/app/output/trajectory.npz")`, which compresses and records the hand. Row `i` holds the motor
targets for physics step `i` after the frozen reset, in `s.actuator_names` order, within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`.
The separate verifier starts from its own frozen scene and replays only these rows in one fresh process, which must succeed. The episode ends at the first success or failure, so rows after
it are not executed. Object poses, success flags or other members of the archive are ignored.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

A single hinge with the arm's servo gains agrees (one 2 ms step from 0.5 rad/s, implicitfast): with the servo on its 18 N m force limit through the actuator's forcerange MuJoCo 3.4.0 gives 0.532847 rad/s, the step with the velocity gain of the servo in the implicit matrix, and MuJoCo 3.8.0 gives 0.536000 rad/s, the step without the velocity gain; far from the limit they give 0.468978 and 0.468978 rad/s.

All four are the expected classes.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Carry a tray with two filled glasses around a bottle to the other counter

Carry the serving tray with the two filled glasses from the source counter (centre x = 0.35 m) to the receiving counter (centre x = 0.78 m). Two dexterous hands, each on its own six-axis wrist stage, start above the two ends of the tray's long axis; the tray rim has open handle slots under the rim bar at both of those ends. Carry the tray around the steel bottle standing on the source counter at (0.52, 0.22) m and across the 30 mm gap between the counters, set it down on the receiving counter and let go. The liquid is not simulated: a glass counts as spilled when its axis tilts more than 15 degrees from vertical. Glass positions are measured in the tray frame, whose origin is the bottom centre of the tray floor (the floor's top surface is at height +2 mm in that frame). A glass is seated when its base centre lies inside the tray footprint ellipse (semi-axes 0.165 m x 0.23 m) and at a height between -3 mm and +8 mm in the tray frame. Success requires, in this order: (1) lift-off: the tray touches neither counter, its base is at least 30 mm above the counter top (z >= 0.91 m) and both glasses are seated; (2) placement: the tray rests on the receiving counter only, its centre within 20 mm in x and 30 mm in y of (0.78, 0.00) m, tray tilt at most 5 degrees, tray yaw within 10 degrees of its start orientation (long axis along y), both glasses seated; (3) release: the placement conditions plus no hand touching the tray or a glass, both glasses within 6 degrees of vertical, tray and glasses at rest (every linear speed at most 0.02 m/s and every angular speed at most 0.2 rad/s), held for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; a partial transfer never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics step, when a glass tilts more than 15 degrees (spilled); a glass base centre leaves the footprint ellipse, or its height in the tray frame exceeds +22 mm (20 mm above the floor's top surface) or falls below -10 mm; the bottle touches the tray, a glass or a hand; the tray touches the source counter again after lift-off; the tray touches the receiving counter while its centre is more than 40 mm in x or 50 mm in y from (0.78, 0.00) m (no dragging); the tray or a glass moves downward faster than 0.6 m/s (dropped; a free fall of about 18 mm), or faster than 0.2 m/s while unsupported (the tray touching no hand and no counter; a glass touching neither the tray, the other glass, a hand nor a counter); the tray tilts more than 35 degrees; the tray or a glass goes below z = 0.86 m, touches the floor or leaves the workspace box x in [0, 1.15] m, y in [-0.6, 0.6] m, z in [0.86, 1.12] m (so the tray cannot be lifted over the bottle); or the physics becomes unstable. Later actions cannot undo a failure. Only actuator targets of the two wrist stages and hands are commanded: no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or applied forces. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.

You control two dexterous hands, each mounted on its own six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three
serial revolute joints, no arm). The left hand hangs above the +y end of the tray, the right hand above the -y end,
fingers pointing down and palms facing the tray. Stages and fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under
native force bounds; lifting, carrying and setting down the tray require physical contact. The controller runs at
50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Two hands of the selected model, each on its own six-axis wrist stage (no arm): the left hand at the +y end of the tray, the right hand at the -y end. Every row holds both stages' targets and both hands' finger targets (layout below).
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`56` for `sharpa`, `52` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

The liquid is not simulated: a glass counts as spilled when its axis tilts more than 15 degrees from vertical. Glass positions are measured in the tray frame, whose origin is the bottom centre of the tray floor (the floor's top surface is at height +2 mm in that frame). A glass is seated when its base centre lies inside the tray footprint ellipse (semi-axes 0.165 m x 0.23 m) and at a height between -3 mm and +8 mm in the tray frame. The episode ends with success at that moment; a partial transfer never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics step, when a glass tilts more than 15 degrees (spilled); a glass base centre leaves the footprint ellipse, or its height in the tray frame exceeds +22 mm (20 mm above the floor's top surface) or falls below -10 mm; the bottle touches the tray, a glass or a hand; the tray touches the source counter again after lift-off; the tray touches the receiving counter while its centre is more than 40 mm in x or 50 mm in y from (0.78, 0.00) m (no dragging); the tray or a glass moves downward faster than 0.6 m/s (dropped; a free fall of about 18 mm), or faster than 0.2 m/s while unsupported (the tray touching no hand and no counter; a glass touching neither the tray, the other glass, a hand nor a counter); the tray tilts more than 35 degrees; the tray or a glass goes below z = 0.86 m, touches the floor or leaves the workspace box x in [0, 1.15] m, y in [-0.6, 0.6] m, z in [0.86, 1.12] m (so the tray cannot be lifted over the bottle); or the physics becomes unstable. Later actions cannot undo a failure. Only actuator targets of the two wrist stages and hands are commanded: no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or applied forces. You control two dexterous hands, each mounted on its own six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three
serial revolute joints, no arm). The left hand hangs above the +y end of the tray, the right hand above the -y end,
fingers pointing down and palms facing the tray. Stages and fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under
native force bounds; lifting, carrying and setting down the tray require physical contact. The controller runs at
50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Two hands of the selected model, each on its own six-axis wrist stage (no arm): the left hand at the +y end of the tray, the right hand at the -y end. Every row holds both stages' targets and both hands' finger targets (layout below).
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `56` wide for `sharpa` and `52` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control and holds, in this order:

1. the left wrist stage: `l_wrist_x, l_wrist_y, l_wrist_z` (metres, displacement along the world axes from the stage
   base at (0.35, 0.272, 1.15) m) and `l_wrist_rx, l_wrist_ry, l_wrist_rz` (radians, serial XYZ hinges at the wrist);
2. the right wrist stage: `r_wrist_x ... r_wrist_rz` (same, stage base at (0.35, -0.272, 1.15) m);
3. the left hand's finger targets, then the right hand's finger targets, in radians:
   - `sharpa`: 56 values; 22 Sharpa Wave finger targets per hand, `l_hand_thumb_CMC_FE ... l_hand_pinky_DIP`, then
     `r_hand_thumb_CMC_FE ... r_hand_pinky_DIP` (the left hand is the mirrored Wave);
   - `wuji`: 52 values; 20 Wuji Hand 2.2 finger targets per hand, `l_wuji_l_THJ0..3, l_wuji_l_FFJ0..3, ...,
     l_wuji_l_LFJ0..3`, then `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3 ... r_wuji_r_LFJ0..3`.

Every target must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`. Both hands start with every target at 0 clipped into its
range (stages at their base pose, open hands).

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 56)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 52)`
for `wuji`, at most 3000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Plug a USB cable into a hub port

Connect the USB cable to the hub. You drive the right arm and hand of a Tianji Marvin robot standing in front of the desk (left arm parked). A four-port USB hub rests free on the desk with its ports facing the desk's front edge (world -y); the cable's USB-A plug lies on its side on the desk, with its 0.5 m cable. Pick up the plug, turn it so its polarized (top) face points up, and insert it into port 4, the rightmost port (hub-local x = +33 mm), then let go. Success requires three stages in order. (1) Grasped and lifted: the thumb and at least one other finger touch the rigid plug (shell, housing or strain relief), the plug touches nothing else, and the plug origin (the centre of its metal shell tip) is at z >= 0.73 m (30 mm above the desk top at z = 0.70 m). (2) Seated in port 4: in that port's frame the shell tip is at least 10.8 mm deep in the 12 mm cavity (90%), within 0.6 mm of the port axis sideways and 0.5 mm vertically, the plug axis is within 5 degrees of the port axis, and the plug's top face is within 20 degrees of the hub's top face (correct polarity). (3) Released: the plug stays seated in port 4 with no hand contact on the plug, its cable or the hub and a plug speed of at most 0.01 m/s for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment. A plug seated in any other port never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure when the hub moves more than 20 mm from its start position or tilts more than 20 degrees, when the plug falls below z = 0.685 m, when the plug or hub leaves the workspace box x in [0.25, 1.15] m, y in [-0.40, 0.95] m, z in [0.685, 1.10] m, when the cable's far USB-B end falls more than 5 cm below the desk top, when an arm link, the robot's stand or torso, or the parked left hand touches anything (`robot_collision`: the desk, the floor, the hub, the plug or cable, the working hand or another robot part), when the plug is dropped (after stage 1, at the first control at which the plug has no hand contact on it or its cable, is not engaged at least 3 mm deep in a port, and either falls faster than 0.2 m/s or lies on the desk or floor), or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed; no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. Each port is an open rectangular cavity with generous clearance (0.25 mm per side across, 0.15 mm per side in height); the receptacle tongue and contacts are visual, and there are no retention springs, so the plug stays in by friction and its own weight. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.

You control the right arm and right hand of a fixed Tianji Marvin robot: a stand with two 7-joint arms and a dexterous
hand on each wrist. The robot stands on the floor in front of the desk, right of the hub (base centre at x = 0.93,
y = -0.52 on the floor at z = -0.20, facing the desk at yaw 135 deg, i.e. toward world (-1, +1)/sqrt(2); shoulders
at z = 1.021 m, 1.221 m above the floor). The left arm stays parked beside the torso with its hand open; the task is done by the right
arm and hand alone. Every arm and finger joint is a position servo inside the physics engine under native force
bounds; arm servos have stiffness 700 N m/rad, damping 48 N m s/rad and **no gravity compensation** (a held target sags
under the arm's weight unless your targets account for it). Grasping, carrying, inserting and releasing require
physical contact. Only the working right hand may touch the desk and the task objects: any contact of an arm link, the
stand or torso, or the parked left hand with anything fails the episode at once (`robot_collision`). The controller
runs at 50 Hz, with ten 2 ms physics substeps.

## Scene
- Desk: top at z = 0.70 m (0.90 m above the floor at z = -0.20), front edge at y = -0.114 m (world frame, z up,
  metres and radians); its two front legs stand back under the top (x 0.32, y 0.00 and x 1.08, y 0.46), clear of
  the robot's base plate.
- Hub: the original four-port USB hub (103 x 30 x 10 mm, 21.8 g) rests free on the desk on rubber pads, its port face
  flush with the desk's front edge and facing -y; it is not fixed or held. Ports 1-4 are at hub-local
  x = -27, -7, +13, +33 mm; port 4 (the target) is the rightmost seen from the front. Its own upstream cable is drawn
  lying on the desk and has no physics.
- Plug: a free USB-A plug (7 g; metal shell 12.0 x 4.5 x 12 mm, housing 15 x 20 x 8 mm, strain relief) lying on its
  side on the desk, with a passive 0.5 m cable (20 ball-jointed links, 15 g) ending in a free USB-B plug on the desk.
  The plug frame origin is the centre of the shell tip; its +y axis points out of the shell (insertion direction)
  and +z is the polarized top face. Inserted correctly, the plug's +y aligns with the hub's +y and +z with the hub's +z.
- Ports are open rectangular cavities 12.5 x 4.8 x 12 mm (0.25 mm clearance per side across, 0.15 mm in height); the
  receptacle tongue and contacts are visual only, polarity is part of the success predicate, and there are no
  retention springs: a seated plug stays by friction and its own weight.
- Cameras: `overview` (desk, hub and plug from the front left) and `closeup` (the hub's port face).

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Each row starts with the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (left arm J1-J7, then right arm J1-J7), followed by the left hand's finger targets and then the right hand's (22 per hand for `sharpa`, 20 per hand for `wuji`); the left arm is parked and only the right arm/hand perform the task.
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`58` for `sharpa`, `54` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

## Hands

Each row starts with the 14 Marvin arm joint targets (left arm J1-J7, then right arm J1-J7), followed by the left hand's finger targets and then the right hand's (22 per hand for `sharpa`, 20 per hand for `wuji`); the left arm is parked and only the right arm/hand perform the task.
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `58` wide for `sharpa` and `54` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control and holds a position target for every actuator, in radians:

- `sharpa` (58 values): 0-6 the left arm `SHOULDER_PITCH_L_J1, SHOULDER_ROLL_L_J2, ELBOW_PITCH_L_J3, ELBOW_YAW_L_J4,
  WRIST_PITCH_L_J5, WRIST_YAW_L_J6, WRIST_ROLL_L_J7` (actuators `<joint>_target`; keep them at the parked start
  values), 7-13 the same right-arm joints (`..._R_J1` to `..._R_J7`), 14-35 the 22 left Sharpa Wave finger targets
  `left_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `left_pinky_DIP`, 36-57 the 22 right Sharpa Wave finger targets `right_thumb_CMC_FE` ...
  `right_pinky_DIP`.
- `wuji` (54 values): 0-13 the same arm targets, 14-33 the 20 left Wuji Hand 2.2 finger targets `l_wuji_l_THJ0..3`,
  `l_wuji_l_FFJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_MFJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_RFJ0..3`, `l_wuji_l_LFJ0..3`, 34-53 the 20 right ones
  (`r_wuji_r_...`, same order).

Every target must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`. The frozen start targets of each hand are in `task.json`
(`initial_targets`); the right hand's frame is the body `wrist_stage` on the right flange (fingers along its +z, palm
normal +x, thumb +y), which forward kinematics of the arm joints places in the world.

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 58)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 54)`
for `wuji`, at most 3000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

dexhand-vacuum-bin-reseat-i00 · upstream folder tasks/dexhand/dexhand-vacuum-bin-reseat-i00-standard

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexHand: Remove and reinstall a vacuum dust bin

Remove the dust bin from the handheld vacuum on the counter and reinstall it. The bin is held by its two lower tabs on ledges at the bottom of the motor housing and by a spring latch at the top: the latch tooth on the red release button stops the bin's top catch from tilting out, and a fixed lip over the catch bridge stops it from being lifted straight out, so the top must tilt out from under the lip, which the tooth only allows while the button is pressed. Stages, in order: (1) release and remove: press the release button by at least 5.8 mm while the bin is still in its seat (bin origin within 5 mm of its seated pose), then take the bin away until its origin is more than 30 mm from its seated pose (both measured in the vacuum-body frame); (2) reinstall: put the bin back so that its origin is within 3 mm and its orientation within 0.05 rad of the seated pose (vacuum-body frame), the release button is back up (travel at most 1.5 mm, latch tooth raised) and the bin's catch is behind the tooth face (at most 0.5 mm in front of it); (3) let go: the stage-2 condition must hold with no hand contact on the bin, the vacuum body or the button, the bin and the vacuum body at rest (linear speed at most 0.01 m/s, bin angular speed at most 0.1 rad/s), for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; partial completion never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 1 ms physics substep, when the vacuum body moves more than 50 mm or tilts more than 0.35 rad from its start pose, when the bin falls (centre-of-mass downward speed above 0.99 m/s, i.e. a free fall from 5 cm, or above 0.55 m/s while nothing touches it), touches the floor or a table leg, its origin drops below the counter top (z < 0.65 m) or leaves the workspace box x in [0.2, 1.1] m, y in [-0.45, 0.45] m, z in [0.6, 1.2] m, when bin and vacuum geometry interpenetrate by more than 4 mm, or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets (the two wrist stages and the fingers of both hands) are allowed; no object teleports, welds or applied forces. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz.

You control two dexterous hands, each mounted on its own six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three
serial revolute joints, no arm): the right hand on the stage `wrist_stage` (origin (0.45, 0.0, 0.8) m) and
the left hand (the right hand's mirror image) on `left_wrist_stage` (origin (0.55, 0.3, 0.95) m).
Both are needed as in the real task: one hand steadies the vacuum (or works the button) while the other handles the
bin. The stages and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under native force bounds; the vacuum
body, the dust bin and the release button move only through contact and their passive dynamics (the button is a spring-loaded
slide). The controller runs at 50 Hz, with twenty 1 ms physics substeps.

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Two hands, each on its own six-axis wrist stage. Sharpa (56): right stage (6), right fingers (22), left stage (6), left fingers (22). Wuji (52): right stage (6), left stage (6), right fingers (20), left fingers (20). The left hand is the right Wave mirrored in y (shared arm_rig.mirrored_left_wave); one row is one 50 Hz control (twenty 1 ms physics substeps).
The robot service runs the hand named by `DEXHAND_HAND` on the sim service (default `sharpa`); the agent cannot switch it during an episode. `spec()["hand"]` names it, and `spec()["action_types"]["joint_position"]` gives the row width (`56` for `sharpa`, `52` for `wuji`) and the exact order. The episode record names the hand; the service grades the episode it ran with that hand.

## Scene and frames
The world frame has z up; lengths are in metres, angles in radians, quaternions WXYZ. A handheld vacuum (free body
`vacuum_body`, 0.752 kg) stands on its base skid on the counter (top at z = 0.65 m); its transparent dust bin (free body
`dust_container`, 0.18 kg) sits in front of the motor housing, with the nozzle overhanging the counter edge. The bin is
held at the bottom by two tabs resting on two ledges inside its mouth and at the top by the latch tooth of the red
release button (`release_button`, spring-loaded slide joint `button_depression`, 0 to 6 mm of travel, 600 N/m; the
source scene's values). The tooth's ramp lets the bin's catch push it down while the bin is closed; pressing the button
(nearly its full 6 mm) lowers the tooth below the catch. Latch tooth, catch and bridge have the source's plastic friction
0.55, so pushing the catch over the raised tooth needs a large closing force. A fixed lip on the housing sits 0.7 mm above the catch's bridge, so the seated bin cannot be
lifted straight out: its top has to tilt out from under the lip, which the raised tooth prevents. The vacuum-body frame is the body frame of `vacuum_body`; the seated bin pose in that frame is
fixed by the frozen start state (the bin starts seated). Cameras: `overview` (the counter
from the front left) and `closeup` (the latch and the bin).

## Episodes and resets
You have **20 resets** (`spec["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0, there is no reset
and the one episode is the run). A reset puts the robot and every object back in the same frozen starting state and
starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended; it takes no simulated time and
returns the start's images and proprioception:
```python
res = r._post("/reset", {"cameras": ["overview"]}, [], 900)   # POST /reset (the 2.2 client has no reset())
res.meta["episode"], res.meta["resets_left"]
```
Once an episode has ended, `submit` raises `EpisodeOver` until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: an
episode you reset away is never graded, a success ends the run at once (no reset after it), and when your time is up
the episode then running is the one graded. The wall clock is the run's and never restarts; `meta["episode"]` and
`meta["resets_left"]` count the episodes (`meta["control_steps"]` is the current episode's,
`meta["control_steps_total"]` all of them).

You control two dexterous hands, each mounted on its own six-DoF wrist positioning stage (three prismatic and three
serial revolute joints, no arm): the right hand on the stage `wrist_stage` (origin `task.json` `wrist_stage.origin`) and
the left hand (the right hand's mirror image) on `left_wrist_stage` (origin `task.json` `left_wrist_stage.origin`).
Both are needed as in the real task: one hand steadies the vacuum (or works the button) while the other handles the
bin. The stages and the fingers are position actuated in the physics engine under native force bounds; the vacuum
body, the dust bin and the release button move only through contact and their passive dynamics (the button is a spring-loaded

## Hands
Two genuine manufacturer hand models are available: `sharpa` (Sharpa Wave, 22 finger actuators; the default) and `wuji` (Wuji Hand 2.2, 20 finger actuators). The task, scene, mount, objects and success predicate are the same for both; only one hand is used per episode.
Two hands, each on its own six-axis wrist stage. Sharpa (56): right stage (6), right fingers (22), left stage (6), left fingers (22). Wuji (52): right stage (6), left stage (6), right fingers (20), left fingers (20). The left hand is the right Wave mirrored in y (shared arm_rig.mirrored_left_wave); one row is one 50 Hz control (twenty 1 ms physics substeps).
Choose the hand with `Session(..., hand="wuji")` or the environment variable `DEXHAND_HAND=wuji` (default `sharpa`). Action rows are `56` wide for `sharpa` and `52` wide for `wuji`; `s.actuator_names` gives the exact order. `s.save_trajectory(actions, path)` records the hand in the archive (`hand` member). The verifier rebuilds the scene with the recorded hand (default `sharpa` when the member is absent) and rejects a trajectory whose width does not match that hand; rows are never padded, truncated or converted between hands.

## Scene and frames
The world frame has z up; lengths are in metres, angles in radians, quaternions WXYZ. A handheld vacuum (free body
`vacuum_body`, 0.752 kg) stands on its base skid on the counter (top at z = 0.65 m); its transparent dust bin (free body

held at the bottom by two tabs resting on two ledges inside its mouth and at the top by the latch tooth of the red
release button (`release_button`, spring-loaded slide joint `button_depression`, 0 to 6 mm of travel, 600 N/m; the
source scene's values). The tooth's ramp lets the bin's catch push it down while the bin is closed; pressing the button
(nearly its full 6 mm) lowers the tooth below the catch. Latch tooth, catch and bridge have the source's plastic friction
0.55, so pushing the catch over the raised tooth needs a large closing force. A fixed lip on the housing sits 0.7 mm above the catch's bridge, so the seated bin cannot be
lifted straight out: its top has to tilt out from under the lip, which the raised tooth prevents. The vacuum-body frame is the body frame of `vacuum_body`; the seated bin pose in that frame is
`task.json` `checker.seat_pos` (metres) and `checker.seat_rot` (row-major 3 x 3). Cameras: `overview` (the counter
from the front left) and `closeup` (the latch and the bin).

## Action layout
Each row is one 50 Hz control holding a position target for every actuator, in native actuator order:

- `sharpa` (56 values): 0-5 the right stage `wrist_x, wrist_y, wrist_z` (metres, offsets from its origin, world axes)
  and `wrist_rx, wrist_ry, wrist_rz` (radians, serial XYZ joints, not a quaternion); 6-27 the 22 right Sharpa Wave
  finger targets `right_thumb_CMC_FE` ... `right_pinky_DIP`; 28-33 the left stage `left_wrist_x` ... `left_wrist_rz`
  (same convention, its hand mounted without rotation); 34-55 the 22 left finger targets `left_thumb_CMC_FE` ...
  `left_pinky_DIP`.
- `wuji` (52 values): 0-5 the right stage, 6-11 the left stage, 12-31 the right Wuji Hand 2.2 fingers
  `r_wuji_r_THJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_FFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_MFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_RFJ0..3`, `r_wuji_r_LFJ0..3`, 32-51 the left
  Wuji fingers in the same order (`l_wuji_l_...`); `s.actuator_names` is authoritative.

Every target must lie within `s.model.actuator_ctrlrange`. The frozen start targets of each hand are in `task.json`
(`initial_targets`).

## Deliverable
Save `/app/output/trajectory.npz` with a finite numeric `actions` array of shape `(T, 56)` for `sharpa` or `(T, 52)`
for `wuji`, at most 3000 rows, plus the `hand` member (`s.save_trajectory` writes both), and
`/app/output/gen.py`, the script that produced it. The separate verifier rebuilds the frozen scene with the recorded
hand and replays only these motor targets in one fresh process, which must succeed. A replay stops at the first success or the first failure; later rows are not executed. Object poses,
configuration overrides, pickled arrays and success claims are not deliverables and are never read.
Save the archive compressed (`numpy.savez_compressed`; `s.save_trajectory` does): an archive file larger than 64 MB is rejected with reward 0.

STANDARD MODE (robot as a service, eai-standard/2.1): DexToolBench (SimToolReal) blue_brush / sweep_forward in MuJoCo: KUKA iiwa 14 + Sharpa HA4 hand; produce one replayable joint-target trajectory that carries the blue brush through the 34 demonstrated goal poses in order. The agent only gets a client: camera RGB-D + proprioception and joint-target chunks; 20 resets (only the last episode graded), no object poses; the sim service records every episode and grades the last one live (no grading replay).
  • Original environment (the benchmark's own code, MuJoCo 3.3.7, run here in its pinned Docker image): the reference reaches 8 of 34 goals; its 823 action rows end there, the result the task's README documents. The start-state hash 635c6e406bb9 equals the one recorded in the task, two fresh runs give identical arrays, and the unmodified replay entry point returns the same result (end hash 208d47bb13b7).
  • The scene without the robot is exported as one file written with full precision (the benchmark has no scene file; its scene is built by code). The rig inside the arena equals the rig compiled alone over 10,016 values, apart from the mount pose of its three root bodies and derived arrays that differ by at most 9.9e-11.

The limits are 1e-12 and 1e-9. Running freely for 2.5 s with the rig held by a servo and touching nothing, the tool's coordinates differ from those in the scene alone by at most 1.0e-15 (the scene alone against itself after a 1e-15 nudge: 1.1e-15).

  • The goal rule with our rig runs unchanged: the benchmark's tracker (the port's copy that reproduced the original bit for bit) reads the tool's pose only. On the arena, with the tool left alone, it counts 0 of 34 goals (closest approach 154 mm, tolerance 15 mm) and ends the attempt by the 30 s per-goal limit at control 1,800; with the tool set by hand to goal 1, 2 and 3 between controls it counts 1, 2, 3 and moves the green marker each time. The same two tests on the scene without any robot and on the original model with its robot idle give the same counts; over the 1,800 free-running controls with the tool left alone, the distance the rule computes differs from the arena's by at most 3.6e-16 m (no robot) and 4.4e-16 m (original robot), against 6.7e-16 m for the scene without a robot against itself after its tool is moved by 1e-15 m; set to the goals, the tool touches the idle original hand in 1 of 3 controls of the original model, which moves it by up to 9.3 mm.

The task was built for a left hand and our policy drives the right hand; the reference actions are joint targets of the original robot and cannot be replayed on ours; nothing here shows that our robot can do the task. The light named top follows the centre of mass of the whole model and so stands 121 mm from where it stood in the original at the reset. The binding self-test, tools/check.py and the task folder are other steps, so the status of this task is not changed here.
Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexToolBench · blue brush · sweep_forward (MuJoCo) — STANDARD MODE (robot as a service)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **blue brush** on it.
**Task:** pick up the blue brush and move it through the demonstrated motion (a forward sweep): bring it to each
of the **34 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `brush / blue_brush /
sweep_forward` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

You control the robot **as if it were real hardware**: the simulator runs in a service you cannot open. You get one
client and **20 resets**: at most 21 episodes, of which the last is graded.

## Rules (real-robot rules)
- **Episodes and resets.** You have **20 resets** (`spec()["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0,
  there is no reset and the one episode is the run). `r.reset()` puts the robot, the tool and the goals back to the same
  starting state and starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended. Within an episode
  nothing is undone: a tool knocked off the table stays there until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: a
  success (every goal reached) ends the run at once, and when your time is up the episode then running is the one
  graded, so do not reset away a good episode late. Resetting does not stop or restore the clock.
- **No privileged state.** You see what the cameras see (RGB, optional depth, with each camera's calibration) plus the
  robot's own joint positions, velocities and targets. No object poses, no success predicate.
- Your only budget is the time limit (`## Time limit`). `meta["time_left_s"]` is the service's count of it, from your first
  request to the service: it never runs out before your time does, so plan by it. There is nothing to hand in: the
  service records every episode, and grades the last one as the trajectory. Leave your script at `/app/output/gen.py` for the
  record.
- Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any published solution for this benchmark; write your own controller.
- Images come back as arrays in a Python object; what you look at and where you store it is up to your code.

## Scoring
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. In this mode goals have **no time limit** (the benchmark gives each goal 10 s). An episode ends when every goal is reached, when your time is up, or after **360,000 control steps (100 min of robot time)**. **Only the last episode is scored.**
**Score: 1 if all 34 goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 34 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.
Full task description (original text, privileged setting; differs from the standard one)
# DexToolBench · blue brush · sweep_forward (MuJoCo)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **blue brush** on it.
**Task:** pick up the blue brush and move it through the demonstrated motion (a forward sweep): bring it to each
of the **34 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `brush / blue_brush /
sweep_forward` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

## What you hand in
`/app/output/trajectory.npz` — joint position targets, shape `(T, 29)`, one row per control step (1/60 s), each held
for 10 physics steps. Record it with the tooling (below) so the layout is right. The verifier replays it from the
frozen start state in a separate sandbox (MuJoCo on CPU is bit-exact) and scores it. Leave the script that produced it
at `/app/output/gen.py`.

## Scoring (the benchmark's own rule)
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. Each goal has **30 s (1,800 control steps)**; if it is not reached in time the attempt ends there (DexToolBench's own rule is 10 s; relaxed here because your trajectory is replayed offline and you can reset as often as you like). The trajectory may be at most 360,000 control steps.
**Score: 1 if all 34  goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 34 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

## Rules
- The network reaches only the model API and the package registries (PyPI, Debian / Ubuntu archives). Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any
  DexToolBench / SimToolReal solution; write your own controller.
- Only the joint targets count: editing `s.data` (e.g. moving the tool by hand) while debugging changes nothing in
  the replay.

# DexToolBench · red brush · sweep_forward (MuJoCo) — STANDARD MODE (robot as a service)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **red brush** on it.
**Task:** pick up the red brush and move it through the demonstrated motion (a forward sweep): bring it to each
of the **38 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `brush / red_brush /
sweep_forward` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

You control the robot **as if it were real hardware**: the simulator runs in a service you cannot open. You get one
client and **20 resets**: at most 21 episodes, of which the last is graded.

## Rules (real-robot rules)
- **Episodes and resets.** You have **20 resets** (`spec()["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0,
  there is no reset and the one episode is the run). `r.reset()` puts the robot, the tool and the goals back to the same
  starting state and starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended. Within an episode
  nothing is undone: a tool knocked off the table stays there until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: a
  success (every goal reached) ends the run at once, and when your time is up the episode then running is the one
  graded, so do not reset away a good episode late. Resetting does not stop or restore the clock.
- **No privileged state.** You see what the cameras see (RGB, optional depth, with each camera's calibration) plus the
  robot's own joint positions, velocities and targets. No object poses, no success predicate.
- Your only budget is the time limit (`## Time limit`). `meta["time_left_s"]` is the service's count of it, from your first
  request to the service: it never runs out before your time does, so plan by it. There is nothing to hand in: the
  service records every episode, and grades the last one as the trajectory. Leave your script at `/app/output/gen.py` for the
  record.
- Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any published solution for this benchmark; write your own controller.
- Images come back as arrays in a Python object; what you look at and where you store it is up to your code.

## Scoring
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. In this mode goals have **no time limit** (the benchmark gives each goal 10 s). An episode ends when every goal is reached, when your time is up, or after **360,000 control steps (100 min of robot time)**. **Only the last episode is scored.**
**Score: 1 if all 38 goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 38 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

# DexToolBench · red brush · sweep_forward (MuJoCo)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **red brush** on it.
**Task:** pick up the red brush and move it through the demonstrated motion (a forward sweep): bring it to each
of the **38 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `brush / red_brush /
sweep_forward` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

## What you hand in
`/app/output/trajectory.npz` — joint position targets, shape `(T, 29)`, one row per control step (1/60 s), each held
for 10 physics steps. Record it with the tooling (below) so the layout is right. The verifier replays it from the
frozen start state in a separate sandbox (MuJoCo on CPU is bit-exact) and scores it. Leave the script that produced it
at `/app/output/gen.py`.

## Scoring (the benchmark's own rule)
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. Each goal has **30 s (1,800 control steps)**; if it is not reached in time the attempt ends there (DexToolBench's own rule is 10 s; relaxed here because your trajectory is replayed offline and you can reset as often as you like). The trajectory may be at most 360,000 control steps.
**Score: 1 if all 38  goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 38 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

## Rules
- The network reaches only the model API and the package registries (PyPI, Debian / Ubuntu archives). Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any
  DexToolBench / SimToolReal solution; write your own controller.
- Only the joint targets count: editing `s.data` (e.g. moving the tool by hand) while debugging changes nothing in
  the replay.

The design's pre-ranking does not separate the candidates here (9,551 of 57,952 have every sample within 0.66 m of the shoulder), so its ties are broken by the design's own preference order measured by inverse kinematics on 8 evenly spaced hand samples; with the tie-break swap.py uses for DexHandExam (distance from the middle of the reach shell) the best of the 20 candidates reaches 8 of those 8. Candidates whose stand or arm bases would stand inside the table or a prop are passed over (4,538 of the 9,551); MuJoCo itself reports no contact between two bodies fixed to the world.

Against the model the original builder constructs with its own robot (compiled here under MuJoCo 3.8.0), 0 of 3,985 scene values differ, besides the world body's gravity-compensation value, which no scene file can carry and which applies no force. The rig inside the arena equals the rig compiled alone over 10,016 values, apart from the mount pose of its three root bodies and derived arrays that differ by at most 1.1e-10.

For information, the design's first protocol (the rig's motors at zero, so that its arms begin to fall during the substep) gives at most 7.8e-18 and 1.9e-14 over the same runs, which would pass too. Running freely for 2.5 s with the rig held by a servo and touching nothing, the tool's coordinates differ from those in the scene alone by at most 1.5e-15 (the scene alone against itself after a 1e-15 nudge: 1.3e-15).

On the arena, with the tool left alone, it counts 0 of 31 goals (closest approach 38 mm, tolerance 15 mm) and ends the attempt by the 30 s per-goal limit at control 1,800; with the tool set by hand to goal 1, 2 and 3 between controls it counts 1, 2, 3 and moves the green marker each time. The light named top follows the centre of mass of the whole model and so stands 90 mm from where it stood in the original at the reset. The binding self-test, tools/check.py and the task folder are other steps, so the status of this task is not changed here.
Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexToolBench · handle eraser · wipe_c (MuJoCo) — STANDARD MODE (robot as a service)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **handle eraser** on it.
**Task:** pick up the handle eraser and move it through the demonstrated motion (wiping the letter C): bring it to each
of the **31 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `eraser / handle_eraser /
wipe_c` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

You control the robot **as if it were real hardware**: the simulator runs in a service you cannot open. You get one
client and **20 resets**: at most 21 episodes, of which the last is graded.

## Rules (real-robot rules)
- **Episodes and resets.** You have **20 resets** (`spec()["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0,
  there is no reset and the one episode is the run). `r.reset()` puts the robot, the tool and the goals back to the same
  starting state and starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended. Within an episode
  nothing is undone: a tool knocked off the table stays there until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: a
  success (every goal reached) ends the run at once, and when your time is up the episode then running is the one
  graded, so do not reset away a good episode late. Resetting does not stop or restore the clock.
- **No privileged state.** You see what the cameras see (RGB, optional depth, with each camera's calibration) plus the
  robot's own joint positions, velocities and targets. No object poses, no success predicate.
- Your only budget is the time limit (`## Time limit`). `meta["time_left_s"]` is the service's count of it, from your first
  request to the service: it never runs out before your time does, so plan by it. There is nothing to hand in: the
  service records every episode, and grades the last one as the trajectory. Leave your script at `/app/output/gen.py` for the
  record.
- Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any published solution for this benchmark; write your own controller.
- Images come back as arrays in a Python object; what you look at and where you store it is up to your code.

## Scoring
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. In this mode goals have **no time limit** (the benchmark gives each goal 10 s). An episode ends when every goal is reached, when your time is up, or after **360,000 control steps (100 min of robot time)**. **Only the last episode is scored.**
**Score: 1 if all 31 goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 31 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

# DexToolBench · handle eraser · wipe_c (MuJoCo)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **handle eraser** on it.
**Task:** pick up the handle eraser and move it through the demonstrated motion (wiping the letter C): bring it to each
of the **31 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `eraser / handle_eraser /
wipe_c` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

## What you hand in
`/app/output/trajectory.npz` — joint position targets, shape `(T, 29)`, one row per control step (1/60 s), each held
for 10 physics steps. Record it with the tooling (below) so the layout is right. The verifier replays it from the
frozen start state in a separate sandbox (MuJoCo on CPU is bit-exact) and scores it. Leave the script that produced it
at `/app/output/gen.py`.

## Scoring (the benchmark's own rule)
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. Each goal has **30 s (1,800 control steps)**; if it is not reached in time the attempt ends there (DexToolBench's own rule is 10 s; relaxed here because your trajectory is replayed offline and you can reset as often as you like). The trajectory may be at most 360,000 control steps.
**Score: 1 if all 31  goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 31 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

## Rules
- The network reaches only the model API and the package registries (PyPI, Debian / Ubuntu archives). Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any
  DexToolBench / SimToolReal solution; write your own controller.
- Only the joint targets count: editing `s.data` (e.g. moving the tool by hand) while debugging changes nothing in
  the replay.

Running freely for 2.5 s with the rig held by a servo and touching nothing, the tool's coordinates differ from those in the scene alone by at most 2.1e-16 (the scene alone against itself after a 1e-15 nudge: 1.0e-15).

Of the 29 goal positions of the task, the knuckle centre of our hand can be brought to 29 (a held tool lay 63 mm from the original knuckle centre in the median). 310 of the 310 hand samples lie outside the 0.36 m inner shell the co-simulation's planners use and 310 within 0.66 m of the shoulder.

# DexToolBench · handle eraser · wipe_smile (MuJoCo) — STANDARD MODE (robot as a service)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **handle eraser** on it.
**Task:** pick up the handle eraser and move it through the demonstrated motion (wiping a smiley face): bring it to each
of the **29 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `eraser / handle_eraser /
wipe_smile` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

You control the robot **as if it were real hardware**: the simulator runs in a service you cannot open. You get one
client and **20 resets**: at most 21 episodes, of which the last is graded.

## Rules (real-robot rules)
- **Episodes and resets.** You have **20 resets** (`spec()["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0,
  there is no reset and the one episode is the run). `r.reset()` puts the robot, the tool and the goals back to the same
  starting state and starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended. Within an episode
  nothing is undone: a tool knocked off the table stays there until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: a
  success (every goal reached) ends the run at once, and when your time is up the episode then running is the one
  graded, so do not reset away a good episode late. Resetting does not stop or restore the clock.
- **No privileged state.** You see what the cameras see (RGB, optional depth, with each camera's calibration) plus the
  robot's own joint positions, velocities and targets. No object poses, no success predicate.
- Your only budget is the time limit (`## Time limit`). `meta["time_left_s"]` is the service's count of it, from your first
  request to the service: it never runs out before your time does, so plan by it. There is nothing to hand in: the
  service records every episode, and grades the last one as the trajectory. Leave your script at `/app/output/gen.py` for the
  record.
- Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any published solution for this benchmark; write your own controller.
- Images come back as arrays in a Python object; what you look at and where you store it is up to your code.

## Scoring
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. In this mode goals have **no time limit** (the benchmark gives each goal 10 s). An episode ends when every goal is reached, when your time is up, or after **360,000 control steps (100 min of robot time)**. **Only the last episode is scored.**
**Score: 1 if all 29 goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 29 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

# DexToolBench · handle eraser · wipe_smile (MuJoCo)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **handle eraser** on it.
**Task:** pick up the handle eraser and move it through the demonstrated motion (wiping a smiley face): bring it to each
of the **29 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `eraser / handle_eraser /
wipe_smile` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

## What you hand in
`/app/output/trajectory.npz` — joint position targets, shape `(T, 29)`, one row per control step (1/60 s), each held
for 10 physics steps. Record it with the tooling (below) so the layout is right. The verifier replays it from the
frozen start state in a separate sandbox (MuJoCo on CPU is bit-exact) and scores it. Leave the script that produced it
at `/app/output/gen.py`.

## Scoring (the benchmark's own rule)
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. Each goal has **30 s (1,800 control steps)**; if it is not reached in time the attempt ends there (DexToolBench's own rule is 10 s; relaxed here because your trajectory is replayed offline and you can reset as often as you like). The trajectory may be at most 360,000 control steps.
**Score: 1 if all 29  goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 29 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

## Rules
- The network reaches only the model API and the package registries (PyPI, Debian / Ubuntu archives). Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any
  DexToolBench / SimToolReal solution; write your own controller.
- Only the joint targets count: editing `s.data` (e.g. moving the tool by hand) while debugging changes nothing in
  the replay.
