# DexToolBench · short screwdriver · spin_vertical (MuJoCo) — STANDARD MODE (robot as a service)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **short screwdriver** on it.
**Task:** pick up the short screwdriver and move it through the demonstrated motion (spinning it about a vertical axis): bring it to each
of the **76 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `screwdriver / short_screwdriver /
spin_vertical` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

You control the robot **as if it were real hardware**: the simulator runs in a service you cannot open. You get one
client and **20 resets**: at most 21 episodes, of which the last is graded.

## Rules (real-robot rules)
- **Episodes and resets.** You have **20 resets** (`spec()["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0,
  there is no reset and the one episode is the run). `r.reset()` puts the robot, the tool and the goals back to the same
  starting state and starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended. Within an episode
  nothing is undone: a tool knocked off the table stays there until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: a
  success (every goal reached) ends the run at once, and when your time is up the episode then running is the one
  graded, so do not reset away a good episode late. Resetting does not stop or restore the clock.
- **No privileged state.** You see what the cameras see (RGB, optional depth, with each camera's calibration) plus the
  robot's own joint positions, velocities and targets. No object poses, no success predicate.
- Your only budget is the time limit (`## Time limit`). `meta["time_left_s"]` is the service's count of it, from your first
  request to the service: it never runs out before your time does, so plan by it. There is nothing to hand in: the
  service records every episode, and grades the last one as the trajectory. Leave your script at `/app/output/gen.py` for the
  record.
- Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any published solution for this benchmark; write your own controller.
- Images come back as arrays in a Python object; what you look at and where you store it is up to your code.

## Scoring
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. In this mode goals have **no time limit** (the benchmark gives each goal 10 s). An episode ends when every goal is reached, when your time is up, or after **360,000 control steps (100 min of robot time)**. **Only the last episode is scored.**
**Score: 1 if all 76 goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 76 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

# DexToolBench · short screwdriver · spin_vertical (MuJoCo)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **short screwdriver** on it.
**Task:** pick up the short screwdriver and move it through the demonstrated motion (spinning it about a vertical axis): bring it to each
of the **76 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `screwdriver / short_screwdriver /
spin_vertical` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

## What you hand in
`/app/output/trajectory.npz` — joint position targets, shape `(T, 29)`, one row per control step (1/60 s), each held
for 10 physics steps. Record it with the tooling (below) so the layout is right. The verifier replays it from the
frozen start state in a separate sandbox (MuJoCo on CPU is bit-exact) and scores it. Leave the script that produced it
at `/app/output/gen.py`.

## Scoring (the benchmark's own rule)
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. Each goal has **30 s (1,800 control steps)**; if it is not reached in time the attempt ends there (DexToolBench's own rule is 10 s; relaxed here because your trajectory is replayed offline and you can reset as often as you like). The trajectory may be at most 360,000 control steps.
**Score: 1 if all 76  goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 76 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

## Rules
- The network reaches only the model API and the package registries (PyPI, Debian / Ubuntu archives). Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any
  DexToolBench / SimToolReal solution; write your own controller.
- Only the joint targets count: editing `s.data` (e.g. moving the tool by hand) while debugging changes nothing in
  the replay.

Full task description (original text, standard setting)
# DexToolBench · flat spatula · serve_plate (MuJoCo) — STANDARD MODE (robot as a service)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **flat spatula** on it.
**Task:** pick up the flat spatula and move it through the demonstrated motion (serving onto a plate): bring it to each
of the **33 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `spatula / flat_spatula /
serve_plate` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

You control the robot **as if it were real hardware**: the simulator runs in a service you cannot open. You get one
client and **20 resets**: at most 21 episodes, of which the last is graded.

## Rules (real-robot rules)
- **Episodes and resets.** You have **20 resets** (`spec()["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0,
  there is no reset and the one episode is the run). `r.reset()` puts the robot, the tool and the goals back to the same
  starting state and starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended. Within an episode
  nothing is undone: a tool knocked off the table stays there until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: a
  success (every goal reached) ends the run at once, and when your time is up the episode then running is the one
  graded, so do not reset away a good episode late. Resetting does not stop or restore the clock.
- **No privileged state.** You see what the cameras see (RGB, optional depth, with each camera's calibration) plus the
  robot's own joint positions, velocities and targets. No object poses, no success predicate.
- Your only budget is the time limit (`## Time limit`). `meta["time_left_s"]` is the service's count of it, from your first
  request to the service: it never runs out before your time does, so plan by it. There is nothing to hand in: the
  service records every episode, and grades the last one as the trajectory. Leave your script at `/app/output/gen.py` for the
  record.
- Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any published solution for this benchmark; write your own controller.
- Images come back as arrays in a Python object; what you look at and where you store it is up to your code.

## Scoring
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. In this mode goals have **no time limit** (the benchmark gives each goal 10 s). An episode ends when every goal is reached, when your time is up, or after **360,000 control steps (100 min of robot time)**. **Only the last episode is scored.**
**Score: 1 if all 33 goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 33 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.
Full task description (original text, privileged setting; differs from the standard one)
# DexToolBench · flat spatula · serve_plate (MuJoCo)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **flat spatula** on it.
**Task:** pick up the flat spatula and move it through the demonstrated motion (serving onto a plate): bring it to each
of the **33 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `spatula / flat_spatula /
serve_plate` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

## What you hand in
`/app/output/trajectory.npz` — joint position targets, shape `(T, 29)`, one row per control step (1/60 s), each held
for 10 physics steps. Record it with the tooling (below) so the layout is right. The verifier replays it from the
frozen start state in a separate sandbox (MuJoCo on CPU is bit-exact) and scores it. Leave the script that produced it
at `/app/output/gen.py`.

## Scoring (the benchmark's own rule)
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. Each goal has **30 s (1,800 control steps)**; if it is not reached in time the attempt ends there (DexToolBench's own rule is 10 s; relaxed here because your trajectory is replayed offline and you can reset as often as you like). The trajectory may be at most 360,000 control steps.
**Score: 1 if all 33  goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 33 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

## Rules
- The network reaches only the model API and the package registries (PyPI, Debian / Ubuntu archives). Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any
  DexToolBench / SimToolReal solution; write your own controller.
- Only the joint targets count: editing `s.data` (e.g. moving the tool by hand) while debugging changes nothing in
  the replay.

# DexToolBench · spoon spatula · flip_over (MuJoCo) — STANDARD MODE (robot as a service)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **spoon spatula** on it.
**Task:** pick up the spoon spatula and move it through the demonstrated motion (flipping something over): bring it to each
of the **40 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `spatula / spoon_spatula /
flip_over` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

You control the robot **as if it were real hardware**: the simulator runs in a service you cannot open. You get one
client and **20 resets**: at most 21 episodes, of which the last is graded.

## Rules (real-robot rules)
- **Episodes and resets.** You have **20 resets** (`spec()["budget"]["reset"]`, which is authoritative: if it says 0,
  there is no reset and the one episode is the run). `r.reset()` puts the robot, the tool and the goals back to the same
  starting state and starts a new episode, either abandoning the running one or after one has ended. Within an episode
  nothing is undone: a tool knocked off the table stays there until you reset. **Only the last episode is graded**: a
  success (every goal reached) ends the run at once, and when your time is up the episode then running is the one
  graded, so do not reset away a good episode late. Resetting does not stop or restore the clock.
- **No privileged state.** You see what the cameras see (RGB, optional depth, with each camera's calibration) plus the
  robot's own joint positions, velocities and targets. No object poses, no success predicate.
- Your only budget is the time limit (`## Time limit`). `meta["time_left_s"]` is the service's count of it, from your first
  request to the service: it never runs out before your time does, so plan by it. There is nothing to hand in: the
  service records every episode, and grades the last one as the trajectory. Leave your script at `/app/output/gen.py` for the
  record.
- Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any published solution for this benchmark; write your own controller.
- Images come back as arrays in a Python object; what you look at and where you store it is up to your code.

## Scoring
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. In this mode goals have **no time limit** (the benchmark gives each goal 10 s). An episode ends when every goal is reached, when your time is up, or after **360,000 control steps (100 min of robot time)**. **Only the last episode is scored.**
**Score: 1 if all 40 goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 40 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

# DexToolBench · spoon spatula · flip_over (MuJoCo)

A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a 22-joint **Sharpa HA4** dexterous hand stands next to a table with a **spoon spatula** on it.
**Task:** pick up the spoon spatula and move it through the demonstrated motion (flipping something over): bring it to each
of the **40 goal poses in order** (the green ghost tool shows the current goal). This is task `spatula / spoon_spatula /
flip_over` of DexToolBench (SimToolReal), run here in plain MuJoCo.

## What you hand in
`/app/output/trajectory.npz` — joint position targets, shape `(T, 29)`, one row per control step (1/60 s), each held
for 10 physics steps. Record it with the tooling (below) so the layout is right. The verifier replays it from the
frozen start state in a separate sandbox (MuJoCo on CPU is bit-exact) and scores it. Leave the script that produced it
at `/app/output/gen.py`.

## Scoring (the benchmark's own rule)
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. Each goal has **30 s (1,800 control steps)**; if it is not reached in time the attempt ends there (DexToolBench's own rule is 10 s; relaxed here because your trajectory is replayed offline and you can reset as often as you like). The trajectory may be at most 360,000 control steps.
**Score: 1 if all 40  goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 40 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

## Rules
- The network reaches only the model API and the package registries (PyPI, Debian / Ubuntu archives). Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any
  DexToolBench / SimToolReal solution; write your own controller.
- Only the joint targets count: editing `s.data` (e.g. moving the tool by hand) while debugging changes nothing in
  the replay.

`/app/output/trajectory.npz` — joint position targets, shape `(T, 29)`, one row per control step (1/60 s), each held
for 10 physics steps. Record it with the tooling (below) so the layout is right. The verifier replays it from the
frozen start state in a separate sandbox (MuJoCo on CPU is bit-exact) and scores it. Leave the script that produced it
at `/app/output/gen.py`.

## Scoring (the benchmark's own rule)
The current goal counts as reached when all 8 corners of the tool's grasp box (0.141 × 0.030 × 0.027 m, scaled by
1.5, in the tool's frame) are within **1.5 cm** of the same corners at the goal pose; then the next goal becomes
current. Each goal has **30 s (1,800 control steps)**; if it is not reached in time the attempt ends there (DexToolBench's own rule is 10 s; relaxed here because your trajectory is replayed offline and you can reset as often as you like). The trajectory may be at most 360,000 control steps.
**Score: 1 if all 48  goals are reached, else 0.** Goals reached / 48 is reported as `progress`; there is no partial credit.

## Rules
- The network reaches only the model API and the package registries (PyPI, Debian / Ubuntu archives). Do not use pretrained manipulation policies or any
  DexToolBench / SimToolReal solution; write your own controller.
- Only the joint targets count: editing `s.data` (e.g. moving the tool by hand) while debugging changes nothing in
  the replay.
